# Handoff: start here

Read this first; it is the whole state. CLAUDE.md has the binding rules and the check commands. CHANGELOG.md (written
from `Defs/AlmanacArticleDefs/Almanac_WhatsNew.xml`) has every round in the player's words. The sections under
"Older history" at the bottom are kept for reference only.

How to run work (the player, 7 November 2026: "you decide when to do simultanious and when one after another"):
pieces in unrelated areas run side by side in worktrees, three at most (the container has 4 cores, and builds and the
test suite slow down when several run at once); pieces in the same area, or that should build on each other, run one
after another, the later one starting from the merged earlier one. The player's bug reports are fixed in the main
tree at once, alongside whatever runs. Each piece is merged as its own release, checks after every merge.

## State (5 November 2026)

- 0.191.2, foraging leaves the bees alone (9 November 2026, the player: "i think the foraging decree also forages beehive
  trees ... any bee related matters shouldn't be involved as these don't immedieatlly generate food"). Alpha Bees' trees
  with a wild hive are plants harvested for a hive with the `Standard` harvest tag, and the game's `IsTree` holds only for
  wood, so `YearFour.Forage` marked them. It now takes only plants whose harvest is food (`IsNutritionGivingIngestible`).
  0.191.3: medicine too is left out (the player: "ok then just focus only on food, no medicine please"); the decree's
  words say so.
- 0.191.1, the colony news only on days that matter (9 November 2026, the player: "the colonist news pop-up should only
  appear if there's something unusual, important, dangerous or requiring my action. the other information should just be
  kept in the journal/log if it's a day without anythign important"). The evening's digest (`NewsComponent.SendNow`)
  sends its letter only when one of its lines is important (`TellWeight.Important`) or bad news (its message type the
  game's negative, threat or death sound: `News.BadNews`), by `TellMath.EveningLetter`; a quiet day's lines go to the
  History tab's message log (`News.Archive`), counted in `Tell.NoteHistory`. Setting "Only on days that matter"
  (`newsOnlyWhenItMatters`, on, under the colony news setting while it is the digest).

- 0.189.0, a full kit for every colonist (9 November 2026), the player's words with a picture of Avila's gear in Nice Inventory Tab (an autopistol and a belt, no melee weapon,
  "No better weapon in storage"): "the mod should also recognize if a pawn has no melee/ranged sidearm equipped and then
  offer one from the inventory. the pawns should always have a ranged and melee weapon, assuming they have no
  restrictions, and suggest/equip them accordingly. also offhand if they have capacity & compatibility". DESIGN.md "A full
  kit for every colonist" has all of it; README "Judging a weapon" and the mod list; the Almanac's "judging a weapon" (a
  new section, prose only, keywords unchanged).
  - The kit, pure (`Weapons/WeaponKitMath.cs`, linked in Tests.csproj): with Simple Sidearms one ranged and one melee weapon
    (one in hand, the other a sidearm), with Dual Wield the off hand; without Simple Sidearms the one weapon in hand. Each
    slot filled, missing or not for them and why (`Kit`, `KitView`, `KitBar`). Restrictions: incapable of violence, no kit;
    can't shoot or a brawler, melee only; an Ideology role's `RoleEffect_NoRangedWeapons`/`NoMeleeWeapons` (new
    `PickColonist.RoleNoRanged`/`RoleNoMelee`, also in `WeaponPickMath.Score`); the game's refusals, faith, heavy weapons
    as before; Simple Sidearms' weights and its own `CanPickupSidearmInstance` (new `PickOption.SidearmCant`, asked of each
    stored weapon light enough); Dual Wield's `CanBeOffHand`/`IsTwoHand`, same kind as the main hand, never beside a
    two-handed one or with a hand or arm missing (`PickColonist.OneHand`).
  - Minimums: a gap is filled under the usual 0.6, but never under 2.0 for them (`Floor`, twice bare hands); a shooter's
    blade must beat their gun's "in melee" blows by 0.3 (`OverBash`); an off-hand weapon must add 0.3 to both hands
    (`OffHandAdds`). The choice among those by the part it plays (`RoleScore`: the "sidearm" situation half, a quick blade
    +0.2, a gun's "kiting" a tenth). With nothing in hand and both kinds missing, the preferred kind goes in hand.
  - Where from: storage; their own pack (a weapon Simple Sidearms doesn't remember, `WeaponMods.Unremembered` read as its
    own unloading reads its memory: `PickKind.Keep`, remembered at once by `InformOfAddedSidearm`); another's spare
    (`Spares`; `PickKind.Spare`, a new job `Rimfolk_TakeSpareWeapon`, `JobDriver_TakeSpareWeapon` in `WeaponSwapJob.cs`:
    walk over, handed over from the pack into an empty hand or the pack, both memories told). Forbidden weapons in storage
    are read now (`PickWeapon.Forbidden`), never suggested, only asked for (`ForbiddenFills`, `Picks.kitAsks`).
  - The colony's choice (`WeaponPickMath.Assign`): hands first (served first in the greedy, any sensible weapon, a move
    that arms one always wins, if need be taking another's upgrade), the other empty slots' weapons kept from upgrades
    (`Reserve`), off-hand colonists keep their main hand this round, sidearm colonists trade only within the kind; then the
    slots filled by `FightWeight` (the front line first when short); then upgrades, trades, a carried sidearm bettered. The
    old off-hand pass and `SidearmFloor` are gone (the kit's now); the sidearm pass only betters a carried sidearm. The
    random-colony test's brute force now puts the kit first, then the gain.
  - Shown: the row's missing case (`CC_WeaponKit_TagMissing`, "No melee weapon: steel hatchet as a sidearm", buttons Keep
    as sidearm, Take from whom); the honest quiet line ("No melee weapon in storage for Avila", under rows too,
    `WeaponNiceMath.Height`'s `gapLine`; tooltip `WeaponKitWords.LookedTip` from `WeaponKitMath.Looked`); the Defenses
    page's kit chips per colonist and "Fill every kit (n)" (`WeaponPick.DoKit`, orders only); the card's "Who should carry
    this" with who lacks the kind first.
  - Colonists fill a gap themselves (`Weapons/WeaponKitSelf.cs`, setting `weaponKitSelf`, "Colonists fill an empty weapon
    slot themselves", on): on the suggestions' hourly slice (no new Sched slot), free time and safe
    (`WeaponAsks.FreeAndSafe(p, false)`, talking not needed), once a day (`WeaponPickBook.fetched`, saved, pruned daily,
    modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`): `StartJob` (not an order) of the game's Equip into an empty hand, Simple
    Sidearms' `EquipSecondary`, Dual Wield's `DW_EquipOffhand`, or a pack weapon remembered; never in place of what they
    hold, never forbidden, never a bonding persona weapon. A line as they pick it up (the job's finish action on success,
    new pool `Rimfolk_Pool_WeaponKitTake`, 28 lines, every age and tone; in ImmersionTests). Asks gain "kit" (14 lines in
    `Rimfolk_Pool_WeaponAsk`), only when they don't fill it themselves; a forbidden weapon asked for gets an inbox row whose
    act allows it.
  - Tests: `Tools/Tests/WeaponKitTests.cs` (162 checks: Avila's case, a melee fighter's gun, every restriction, without
    Simple Sidearms, nothing at all, the pack, a spare, kit before upgrades and the front line first, the off hand,

    colonist too" on: it's back. 5. Her card: the same two bars. 6. RimHUD: the strain line reads "Worn 60 · fighting",
    whole in its tooltip; the strain bar's value "60".

- 0.187.0, armour and apparel you can judge at a glance, step 1: the rating, its tags and a review of every piece (9
  November 2026, `docs/design/apparel.md` points 1 to 4). No game-side code: only pure math that builds into the mod, the
  tools and the docs. The player's tier-list page is https://claude.ai/artifact/KSfcbX8Pfojbb7cgzZ63T7 (built from
  `docs/apparel/apparel.json` the way the weapons' page was).
  - The rating (`Source/ColonyCouncil/Apparel/ApparelRateMath.cs`, pure; the scale's shape, the reference fighters and
    the ability values from `WeaponRateMath`): a piece worn alone by the weapon review's colonist (Shooting and Melee 8,
    an assault rifle or a steel longsword) at normal quality in its usual stuff (fabric devilstrand, metal steel, leather
    plain leather, wood, granite), and in the common stuffs of its kind. Protection: the game's armour roll layer by
    layer (`ArmorUtility`: a sharp hit halved goes on as blunt, armour held at 200%) on the human body's 17 zones (where
    shots, blows and blunt blows land by the game's coverage; a head hit counts double), against 12 raider guns, 7 melee
    weapons, 6 animals, 7 mechanoid attacks and fire (guns 45%, melee 15%, animals 15%, mechanoids 20%, fire 5%).
    The fight = toughness (bare damage over damage worn) x output (aim, melee hit, cooldown, a shield that stops shooting,
    powers) x feet. A shield takes its share of 6 ranged damage a second over a 30-second fight, at most 85%; powers
    (jump, smoke, low shield, firefoam, grenades, lances, targeters, summons) once a fight by `WeaponRateMath`'s ability
    value, together at most half the output. Everything else (cold, heat, work, social, mind, psychic, mech, magic, toxic,
    vacuum, carry, hunting) is a share of a colonist per stat point (the table in the README). Roles, judged in plain
    stuff: body armour, helmet, off-hand shield, utility, cold- and hot-weather gear, hazard gear, everyday clothing,
    headgear, ceremonial or psychic (children's pieces in their own table); each weighs the areas its own way and has
    its own middle and width; rating = 1 + 9 x `WeaponRateMath.Spread`(ln(worth / middle) / width).
  - Two wearers: every piece is rated for the shooter and for the melee fighter (`OverallShooter`, `OverallMelee`;
    `ratingShooter`, `ratingMelee` in apparel.json, for step 3's per-colonist picks). It clearly suits one when it blocks
    shooting, is an off-hand shield, or does a tenth more for one (toughness x output, the walk left aside so slow armour
    isn't a shooter's for being heavy: `ApparelRateMath.SuitsGap`); then its overall is that wearer's rating, tagged "For
    shooters" or "For melee fighters" with the other side's cost first among its weaknesses ("Spoils your aim", "Blocks
    shooting", "Clumsy in melee"). Else the mix, a shooter's fight three to one. 454 pieces suit both, 39 a melee fighter
    (shield belts, off-hand shields, jump packs, VFE Medieval 2's heavy helmets), 16 a shooter (the gunlink, aim helmets,
    quivers and ammo packs). The README's tables show both ratings where they differ by half a point.
  - Clothing made as armour (its stuff's armour counting at 40% or more) that is rated with clothing is named for what it
    is: "Armour for the hands", "Armour for the feet", "Armour for the head", "Armoured cloak" (in the role tag's place on
    everyday clothing, and in its line: "a poor piece of armour for the hands"); other roles get "Made as armour" beside
    theirs. The role rule itself is unchanged (plate gloves and boots miss body armour's 45% line).
  - The tags (`ApparelTagMath.cs`, pure): the weapons' one table of kinds, colours and symbols (`WeaponTagMath.Categories`,
    shared, not copied); 116 tags, each from a threshold rule with the reason in the piece's own numbers, 3 to 7 per
    piece, most important first; a line in plain words.
  - The mods' code (decompiled with ilspycmd 9.1 into the scratchpad, never run): VEF's off-hand shields (usable only
    with a weapon Dual Wield takes in the off hand), shield bubble and field and apparel extension, A RimWorld of Magic's
    enchantments, VAE Accessories, Fairycore, Vanilla Psycasts Expanded, VFE Empire, Field Medic, Rimatomics, Rimsenal
    Security and MVCF's mini-turrets. What can't be valued (PokeWorld's code isn't in the upload) is named and marked rough.
  - Tools: `Tools/apparel_extract.py` (to `docs/player-mods/apparel_numbers.json.gz`: 512 pieces, the stuffs, the body's
    zones, the reference enemies' weapons and races, title and faith apparel rules, hediffs, the patches that touch a
    piece); `Tools/weapon_extract.py`'s `patches()` takes the parts and stats to look for (the weapon file it writes is
    unchanged byte for byte); `Tools/ApparelReview/` (shares the pure files and the tests' anchors, checks the rating's
    own copies of the body and the enemies against the defs) writes `docs/apparel/README.md` and `docs/apparel/apparel.json`
    (weapons.json's shape plus situations, the rating by stuff, role, layers, body groups, cold and heat ratings, titles,
    faiths, gender, ages, patches).
  - Counts: 512 defs, 509 rated, 3 left out (they vanish when taken off: two mechanoid shield units, a disposable oxygen
    pack), 63 rough, 32 hard to get. Patches touching 20 pieces are listed, not applied.
  - Anchors (in the tests): flak vest 3.9, flak pants 2.1, flak jacket 3.2, plate 4.5, recon 6.8, marine 7.1, cataphract
    7.5; simple helmet 3.5, flak 4.3, recon 7.1, marine 7.2, cataphract 7.4; shield belt 7.6 (for a melee fighter; 1.0
    for a shooter), jump pack 7.2 (a melee fighter's; 4.3 for a shooter), low-shield pack 5.9, smokepop 3.5; parka 7.1 as
    cold-weather gear (1.3 against guns), tribalwear 7.5 everyday (1.4), duster 6.5 hot-weather; gunlink 7.9 (a
    shooter's; 1.0 for a melee fighter), VFE Medieval 2's heavy plate helmet 1.0 (a melee fighter's, 1.0 for both), VAE's
    plate gloves 1.0 ("Armour for the hands"). The flak vest above the flak jacket is the numbers' honest answer (100%
    sharp over the torso against 55% over torso and arms), said in the README.
  - Tests: `Tools/Tests/ApparelRateTests.cs` (205 checks: the roll, the zones, layers, the cap, shields and powers, roles,
    the anchors' order and bands, stuff, the scale, the two wearers, the tags' vocabulary, colours and rules).
  - Soft spots to look at in step 2: VFE Medieval 2's heavy helmets rate 1.0 even for a melee fighter (their 2 levels off
    melee hit, about 8% less damage dealt, outweigh a helmet's armour, about 2% longer in a fight: by the game's roll the
    head takes 6% of shots and 8% of blows; counting head hits for more than double is the lever if that is wanted);
    code-only packs (VFE Deserters', Rimsenal's fortification and omnifoam packs) rate 1.0 rough.

- 0.185.0, the heart, made to count (9 November 2026, release 2 of `docs/design/heart-felt.md`, points 9 to 14; the player's words: "if the strain is not noticeable it
  doesn't make too much sense. also include recommendations and advice on potential actions i can take to reduce strain
  ... i could for example also just grant a single stained pawn a break day"), with their two requests for the same
  screens built beside it: the Mood tab at a glance first, and RimHUD brought to match ("review the "mood" uI for
  colonists, so the most relevant details for strain and mood are visible at first glance ... also perhaps revisit the
  rimui integration"). DESIGN.md "The heart, made to count" has all of it (and Layer 7's bands, "The heart's good side");
  `docs/design/heart-felt.md` release 2 marked built with its choices; README "Feelings and strain" (the bands, felt as it
  should be, a bad afternoon, hearts spread, what would help, a day off you give, where to see it) and the RimHUD lines;
  the Almanac's "feelings and strain" (the bands with the old numbers as the mild choice, a bad afternoon, a day off you
  give, hearts spread a little, what would help, where to see it) and "the heart's good side", prose only, keywords
  unchanged. The balance report was written again (the illness tables by hand kept), with a new section "The heart,
  made to count".
  - What: **stronger bands** (9): strain -4, -8, -14, the good side +3, +6, +10 (the thoughts' stages; the setting
    `heartBands` sizes them in code through the thought's `BaseMoodOffset`: Mild is release 1's, Strong -5, -10, -18 and
    +4, +8, +13); the good side stays in good things growing ordinary's sum as a lasting good mood (no exemption, as it
    was). The bands' own words carry what they do by the settings (`{EFFECTS}`). **Effects beyond mood** (10): stat parts
    in the heart's pattern (`Patches/Council_Heart.xml`, conditional): work 3%, 7%, 12% slower from strained (5%, 10% from
    worn with the setting off), learning (worn 6%, near breaking 10% slower; in good heart 4%, high spirits 8% faster),
    the need for sleep (6%, 10% more), healing (5%, 10% slower; 3%, 6% faster), immunity (3%, 5% slower, never more, tested
    at every pair of bands; 2%, 5% faster); each in the stat's explanation, the bands' words, the card and the Mood tab.
    **A bad afternoon** (11): from 55, hours 12 to 16, 1 in 50 an hour rising to 1 in 25 at 85, a week for each colonist
    and two days in the colony, under the day off's safety rules (`HeartTimeOff.Unsafe`, `Episodes.Busy`, `Episodes.Nursing`);
    three to five hours off work through their timetable: a while beside their bed (a new act, `Cry`), looking out, a drink
    if they drink (`FirstPot.WillDrink`, never addicted or just clean), the grave or the lost one's bed when grieving; a
    message with why, a line; danger ends it; 30% of strain eased (half cut short). **Hearts spread** (12): partners 1, kin
    0.8, friends by opinion 0.4 to 0.8 (`HeartCountMath.Closeness`), 0.06 an hour from someone worn, 0.1 near breaking, 0.15
    an hour and 2.5 a day at most, never past 45 (`SpreadCeiling`); high spirits lift 0.05 an hour (at most 0.1) as a good
    thing; new `StrainSource.Spread`, `StrainRelief.Lifted`, `GoodSource.Lifted` at the ends of their lists, padded.
    **Advice** (13, `Heart/HeartAdvice.cs`): ranked from the heart's sources lately and how they are now
    (`HeartCountMath.Rank`): a day off, the council's decrees that ease strain (days of rest; and the eight that name in
    their defs what they ease, do and cost: `heartEases`, `heartHelp`, `heartCost` on festival days, quiet hours, mourning,
    shared meals, rest when ill, a feast day, a work song, holy days), a gathering, a friend, a meal, a bed, recreation
    (naming what they're tired of), pain, a rest from fighting, grieving, light; buttons: give the day off, propose (the
    colonist's petition through `DecreeTracker.Petition`, the council's own path, then the Decrees page), call a party
    (the game's), send a friend over (`HeartActs.FriendVisit`, a deep talk when the two meet). Built hourly, unsaved. On the
    Mood tab, the card (a section with buttons, the day off among its acts), the message when worn down, the Moods page for
    the colony, RimHUD's tooltip. **A day off** (14, `Heart/HeartTimeOff.cs`): from strained (the choice: a button on every
    colonist would crowd the bar), from the gizmo on a selected colonist, the card, the Mood tab or the advice; a day of
    Work/Anything hours as recreation and a two-hour lie-in, and a think-tree node of Rimfolk's own
    (`Defs/HeartDefs/Rimfolk_Heart_TimeOff.xml`, at `Humanlike_PreMain`: emergency work first, food and sleep, an act now
    and then, recreation, a wander; standing down when drafted, downed, needing a doctor or in danger); rest a quarter
    faster and 0.3 an hour besides, 12 more at its end (half cut short); once in five days; danger ends it every slice;
    the hours changed are saved and put back only where nobody changed them (the calendar's rest day's taken over). **The
    Mood tab** (`Moods/MoodGlance.cs`, `ITab_Pawn_Mood.cs`): the top is the mood and where it heads with the break lines,
    the heart now with today's move and the weight under it in the bar line's colours, what weighs and lifts most (the top
    three across the game's, mods' and Rimfolk's moods, the heart's two with their causes), what each side does now, and
    the top advice with buttons; below, folding sections remembered between sessions (`Folds.Remembered`, PageMemory):
    every mood, the heart, feelings, needs, grown ordinary, lately. **RimHUD**: the strain line reads like the summary
    (both sides in colour, the top cause, time off), its tooltip leads with the advice, a click opens the Mood tab; the
    strain bar says time off; new widgets `Council_Hud_GoodBar` and `Council_Hud_HeartAdvice`. Its DLL isn't needed: only
    the hooks the integration already used (value and bar widgets by name, `GetParameters(Pawn)`).
  - Code: new `Heart/HeartCountMath.cs` (pure, linked in Tests.csproj and Balance.csproj), `Heart/HeartTimeOff.cs` (the
    time off, its think node and job giver, the gizmo patch), `Heart/HeartAdvice.cs`, `Moods/MoodGlance.cs`,
    `Defs/HeartDefs/Rimfolk_Heart_TimeOff.xml`, `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_HeartCounts.xml`. Touched: `HeartMath` (new
    sources, the bands through the new math), `HeartEffects` (the stat parts, `HeartEffects.Doing`), `GoodHeart`,
    `HeartLogic` (spreading, lift, the day off's rest, the bad afternoon from the hour), `HeartData`, `HeartTracker` (the
    slice check), `HeartActs` and `HeartActJob` (the time off's jobs, the `Cry` act), `HeartFelt` (advice in the message),
    `HeartView` (the heart's page split into three sections, the colony's advice, the HUD value), `HeartCard`, `HeartDebug`,
    `Episodes`, `Decrees.cs` (`heartEases`, `heartHelp`, `heartCost`, `Petition`), `UI/RimfolkTab.cs` (remembered folds),
    `Integrations/RimHud.cs`, `CouncilSettings`, `SettingsCatalog` (light touch: mild bands, no bad afternoons); defs: the

    mild bands' runs, breaks by the game's lines); `Tools/save_estimate.py` models `offHours`.
  - Settings (How hard, under the heart's): `heartBands` "How strongly the bands are felt" (Mild, Felt, Strong; Felt),

    no Sched slot.
  - Measured (`Tools/Tests/HeartFeltTests.cs`, 40 runs a case; the release 1 targets still held: calm steady on day 6, in
    good heart on day 18; a friend's death 7.1 days strained, a partner 9.8; a plague season all worn, 4 of 160 near
    breaking): breaks by the game's own lines (35%, 20%, 5%; mean times 4, 0.8, 0.5 days) a colonist-year, felt against mild
    bands: a calm colony 0.00 and 0.00, a plague season 0.32 and 0.14 (under the minor line 2.1% against 1.0%), real
    disasters 0.55 and 0.27; bad afternoons none in a calm colony, 0.34 a colonist-year in a plague season, 154 among 320
    colonists after a disaster; a day off at strain 61 eases 45 in the day against 30 on an ordinary one (43 against 30 with
    a weight of 30 under it); one colonist held near breaking eight weeks among seven close friends: none ever worn down,
    spread 1.0 a day each. Balance simulator (`docs/balance-report.md`, "The heart, made to count", 6 colonists, felt
    against mild): well run no breaks either way, bad afternoons 0.01; average breaks 0.01 and 0.00, strained/worn/near
    breaking 14/4/1%, bad afternoons 0.26, day off at 85 0.10 (0.14 in release 1); neglectful under the minor line 46%
    against 35%, breaks 9.8 against 6.3, bad afternoons 1.38, day off at 85 1.21 (1.6 in release 1). Off target: Rimfolk's
    mood well run +7.3 (target +3 to +6) and +12 or more 29% of the time (rare before): the good side's +3, +6, +10 as the
    player asked; growing ordinary still takes its share. The neglected colony's time under the minor line (46%) is above

  - Riskiest (none of it could be run here): the think-tree node at `Humanlike_PreMain` (that it keeps them from ordinary

- 0.184.0, weapons you can judge at a glance, step 3: the best weapon for each colonist, colonists who ask, and Rimfolk's
  card first (9 November 2026, `docs/design/weapons.md` points 8 and 9 and the player's "can the rimworld weapon card be
  the default screen"). DESIGN.md
  "Step 3: the best weapon for each colonist, and colonists who ask" has all of it; README "Judging a weapon" and the mod
  list; the Almanac's "judging a weapon" (prose only, keywords unchanged).
  - The choice, pure (`Weapons/WeaponPickMath.cs`): a score per colonist and weapon (their own rating, passion 0.15/0.3,
    the situations they meet weighed by the colony's raids and their work, a hunter's 0.8 loss, faith's 0.4); never what
    the game refuses, too heavy, despised, a gun for a brawler or a non-shooter. Threshold 0.6 (asks 1.2); another kind
    +0.5, a bonded persona weapon left unused +1.0 with its cost said. One assignment: greedy by gain, then exchanges
    (pairs, a better leftover, a weapon moved on so a second colonist can have one), then trades better for both (0.3
    each, 0.8 together), then Simple Sidearms' sidearms (its default weights) and Dual Wield's off hands. Reasons: two, the
    strongest first, then costs; keyed words (`CC_WeaponPick_Why_*`).
  - The colony's fights: Rimfolk's own record of raids (`WeaponPickBook.raids`, a hook on
    `IncidentWorker_Raid.PostProcessSpawnedPawns`: how many, mechanoids, armoured, siege, tribe; the last 12) and the game's
    ThreatBig letters for what it lacks; a defense line drawn is a gate held. Defense lines assign no posts, so none are read.
  - In the game (`Weapons/WeaponPick.cs`): home map colonists (grown, not slaves or quest guests), what they hold and carry,
    storage (stockpile, shelf, outfit stand; not forbidden), the 16 best kinds of gun and blade; ratings kept an hour and
    worked out ahead a tenth of the colony every 250 ticks (`Sched.RareWeaponPicks` 47, `Pass.RareWeaponPicks`); the choice
    kept per map, made again hourly, after an order, or when what they hold or the weapon count changes. Orders are real
    jobs: `Equip`, Simple Sidearms' `EquipSecondary` (its `CanPickupSidearmInstance` asked), Dual Wield's `DW_EquipOffhand`,
    and `Rimfolk_SwapWeapons` (`WeaponSwapJob.cs`: one walks to the other, they hand each other their weapons; Simple

- 0.182.0, weapons you can judge at a glance, step 1: the rating, its tags and a review of every weapon (9 November 2026,
  the player's request in `docs/design/weapons.md`). No game-side code yet: only pure math that builds into the mod, the
  tools and the docs; the review is published as a tier-list page for the player.
  - The rating (`Source/ColonyCouncil/Weapons/WeaponRateMath.cs`, pure): a weapon in a fight by the game's own rules (1.6,
    decompiled: ShotReport's hit chance, ArmorUtility's roll, VerbProperties' cycle, explosions' scatter, blast and fuse,
    VerbUtility's melee choice with the fists in the running, stuns that don't stack and EMP adaptation), against a
    reference colonist (Shooting and Melee 8) and five reference enemies from the game's defs (plain clothes; flak vest,
    pants and helmet; marine armour; a lancer and a centipede), hits shared over armour pieces by the human body's
    coverage. Ranged: normalised damage per second at 5, 12, 25 and 40 cells, weighed by role (close, all-round, long,
    area, one-use, anti-mechanoid, utility), a crowd, reach (a quarter off at 12 cells' range, damage past 31 cells
    doubled), punch (heavier hits up to a third more), stopping power, friendly fire; melee by the enemy mix (light under
    1.5 kg, heavy from it). Passives count (accuracy and melee hit as skill, aim and cooldowns in the cycle, move speed,
    dodge, deflection, damage taken, pain); abilities count when readable (spread over a minute, at most half again the
    weapon's own worth). The scale is a Laplace curve in the log of the value, a middle and width per kind, so mods'
    super-weapons land at 9-something. Outputs: the overall, sub-ratings, situations (mechanoids, crowds, hunting, indoors,
    holding a choke, kiting, a siege, capture alive, a sidearm, in melee), damage per second by distance and enemy, specials
    with counted or not and a sign, tags, best for and weak when, the skill it rewards (`SkillGain`).
  - The tags (`WeaponTagMath.cs`, pure; the player's follow-up "tags/labels ... color coded"): 60 tags in six categories
    (strength, weakness, risk, special, role, needs), each a colour from `SkinMath`'s own tokens (Done, Danger, Foe, World,
    Ally, Cool: 4.5:1 on every ground, tested) and a symbol; every tag by a rule on the weapon's numbers with a line saying
    why, at most seven by importance, keeping the role, the first strength and weakness. Sidearm, Offhand and Two-handed
    follow Simple Sidearms' default preset (melee 1.9 kg, ranged 2.7 kg) and Dual Wield's defaults, read from their code.
    The shapes are not weapon-only, for armour and apparel later.
  - Anchors (normal quality, steel): short bow 2.9, revolver 4.5, bolt-action 4.9, assault rifle 5.8, LMG 6.0, sniper 6.4,
    charge lance 6.4, charge rifle 6.7, minigun 6.9, frag grenades 5.7, triple rocket 6.9; knife 4.0, gladius 4.3,
    longsword 5.2, uranium longsword 5.5, plasteel longsword 6.7, uranium mace 6.9, zeushammer 7.4, monosword 7.6.
  - The review: `Tools/weapon_extract.py` (reads the collection through `mod_pool.py`'s new `Pool` class, which
    `mod_pool.py`'s own tables now use too, output unchanged) writes `docs/player-mods/weapon_numbers.json.gz`;
    `Tools/WeaponReview` (net8, links the two math files, `SkinMath.cs` and the test anchors) writes
    `docs/weapons/README.md` and `docs/weapons/weapons.json` (one weapon a line). 747 defs: 486 rated, 1 not rated
    (Winter's Reign, its attack wholly its own code), 260 left out (turret guns, mechanoids' and animals' built-in weapons,
    spell weapons). 72 marked rough: 47 unique weapons (rolled traits) and 25 effects named but not valued (Rimsenal's
    crucible, VWE Non-Lethal's tear gas, darts and taser, the cryptoforge's slowing and others whose code wasn't uploaded).
    25 are tagged Hard to find: no recipe in the player's game and no faction carries them (Possessed Weapons' 16, the
    three Melee Weapons For All polehammers its author left ungated, Ruunbled and a few more).
  - The pool honours `MayRequire` (all of) and `MayRequireAnyOf` (any of) as the game does (LoadedModManager,
    DirectXmlToObject, XmlInheritance; the game and its DLCs always loaded, ids without case or `_steam`): a def that needs
    a package the player hasn't loaded is left out, so is every element inside a def that does, and an abstract parent
    with such a `MayRequire` can't be inherited from. Rebuilt with the 9 November save: 335 defs left out (248 of active
    mods: 158 clutter hand defs, 28 ThingDefs, 26 recipes and others), among them 21 weapons (Melee Weapons For All's
    tenebral, kwazaari and solar weapons, which need BOR) and 6 apparel; 173 rows lost a gated child (a weapon tag, a comp,
    a research, a pawn kind's tags). Poolcheck: Rimfolk's Kiln Guild arms (ages 2 and 3) name Bamba's
    `CE_OneHandedWeapon` tag, which Bamba itself gates on Combat Extended, so no weapon carries it in the player's game
    (Bamba's blades carry no weapon tag without CE). The lines are soft and draw nothing; the other tags in them carry the
    kit. With the catalogue read right, 4 checks in the full suite failed on it (PeoplesETests and PeopleAgesTests:
    every tag must be in the player's active mods); the two lines were dropped at the merge (the guild arms as before).
  - The mods' code (uploaded DLLs, decompiled with `ilspycmd` into the scratchpad, never run; VEF's 1.7 DLL trips the
    project writer, read as IL) moved 40 weapons from rough to counted: VEF's streams and gauss slugs, laser capacitors,
    firing modes; VFE Medieval's matchlocks; A RimWorld of Magic's bolts, wands, cleave and deflectors (and its Light and
    Dark armour, which ordinary armour doesn't give); VWE Bioferrite's incinerator and abilities; dynamite's fuse; the
    game's own beams, fire arrow and doomsday rocket. `MayRequire` list items of inactive mods are now skipped.
  - Tests: `WeaponRateTests` (149 checks: the game's rules, the scale, the anchors' bands and order, specials, passives,
    abilities, the mods' rules, the tag vocabulary, its colours and its rules).
  - Next (step 2, `docs/design/weapons.md`): the weapon card and the weapon mods. The game side feeds `WeaponRateMath` the

- 0.181.0, the heart, felt: it rises and stays, both sides at once, and it shows on the map (9 November 2026, release 1 of
  `docs/design/heart-felt.md`, points 1 to 8; the player's words: "i feel like this impact of strain and all the emotions
  is currently neglible, or hardly noticeable", and on the proposal: "the good side should also be able to develop at the
  same time, not only when strain is at 0"). The balance report was written again with it (the illness tables by hand
  kept). DESIGN.md "The heart, felt: it rises and stays, both sides at once, and it shows on the map" has all of it
  (and Layer 7's strain and good side bullets, "The heart's good side": both sides at once, what fills it, the words);
  `docs/design/heart-felt.md` release 1 marked built with its choices and what wasn't built; README "Feelings and strain"
  (heavy things stay, the good side, on the map); the Almanac's "feelings and strain" (heavy things, rest, on the map, the
  bands beside each other) and "the heart's good side" pages, prose only, keywords unchanged.
  - What: **the lasting weight** (`Heart/HeartFeltMath.cs`, pure; `Heart/HeartFelt.cs`): a death or loss by the game's
    memory (the heaviest of each person, once in three days: partner or family 58, family seen dying 50, a friend 45, a
    bonded animal 28, any colonist 12, someone taken 10 to 30), being downed 22, and while it lasts their own sickness
    that can kill (12 to 52), someone close badly ill (14 to 50 from a third of the way), a fight at home with ours down
    (12 and 8 each, 36 at most); rest can't take strain below it, strain sinks toward it within a day (2.5 an hour,
    "heavy things", `StrainSource.Heavy` at the end of the list), it lifts slowly then faster, good things lift it a
    little, the weights alone never past 76. **Rest under strain**: in full up to 30, 70% from 90. **Both sides at once**:
    the good side grows at any strain (`Growth`: in full up to 10, 30% from 85), good things ease strain and fill it
    together (`Settle`, 35% to the good side), hardship spends 35% of itself from the good side as a cushion
    (`HeartMath.Spend`, `CushionShare`), both band moods apply, and both are shown: the inspector line ("Heart: worn down,
    in good heart · grieving"), RimHUD, the card's Now slot, the Moods page, the tooltips (the strain tooltip's weight
    line, the good side's "grows at 60% of its pace"). **Acts** (`Heart/HeartActs.cs`, `HeartActJob.cs`,
    `Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_HeartActs.xml`, eleven jobs): strained, sitting or looking out; worn, a step outside from ordinary
    work, pacing at night, a short word; in good heart humming at work and lingering at the table; in high spirits singing
    and dancing at a gathering; strong feelings: grief at the grave (the small habit's own) or where the one lost slept,
    fear indoors near someone after dark, anger's sharp word or slammed door, love beside a partner, homesickness at the
    evening's fire (or the small habit's look out), joy shared with a friend (`Together.When`). Safe and free only, one a
    colonist in 16 hours and one in the colony in 3. **Lines** (`Rimfolk_Pool_HeartBand`, 97 lines, and
    `Rimfolk_Pool_HeartAct`, 84): when a band turns and now and then while it holds, naming the cause ("I keep setting a
    place for Ana."), through the touches' one rate. **A sign over the head** (the game's thought bubble, ten shapes in
    `Textures/ColonyCouncil/Icons/Feelings` drawn by `Tools/make_feeling_icons.py`, tinted by the feeling). **The bar's
    heart line** under each name (`BarBadges.HeartLine`, `BarBadgeMath.HeartLine`). **Messages** when worn down or near
    breaking (with why), back from it, in good heart or high spirits (with what filled it), never twice for a hover.
  - Code: new `Heart/HeartFeltMath.cs` (pure, linked in Tests.csproj and Balance.csproj), `Heart/HeartFelt.cs` (the
    weight, `Tell`, `Lines`, `BandLine`, `Sign`, `FeelingIcons`), `Heart/HeartActs.cs`, `Heart/HeartActJob.cs`. Touched:
    `HeartMath` (the cushion, `StrainSource.Heavy`), `HeartLogic` (the hour: the weight, the sink, `Settle`, the map
    after; `EaseJoys` through `Settle`; `Change` lifts the weight), `GoodHeart` (`Fill` at any strain, `Growing`,
    `SlowerLine`), `HeartData`, `HeartTracker` (the map's sick and downed), `HeartView`, `HeartCard`, `HeartDebug` (four
    dev actions), `ColonistBar/BarBadges.cs`, `BarBadgeMath.cs`, `Touches/VisualTouches.cs` (`Notes`),
    `Social/Family.cs` (the bed of the dead for grief), `CouncilSettings`, `SettingsCatalog`; keys in
    `Rimfolk_HeartFelt.xml`, the good side's and strain's explanations updated; `Tools/DefValidator` knows `{SICK}`;
    `Tools/Balance/HeartSim.cs` brought to the new rules.
  - Settings (each on, the heart's How hard page; the bar's line in the colonist bar's): `heartActs` "Small acts by how

    the head for a strong feeling", `heartMessages` "Messages when a heart turns", `barHeartLine` "Heart line under each
    portrait". Saved: values on the heart (`weight`, `weightUntil`, `weightWhy`, `weightAbout`, `weightKind`, `held`,

- 0.180.0, the shared illness budget made soft (9 November 2026, the player's answer to how 0.177.0 works, "Rimfolk's illnesses
  take a turn instead of adding one": "people should be able to suffer for different things, but it should just not be
  common"; the lead's brief: Rimfolk's kinds met regularly, now and then two things at once, even on one person, serious
  illness in all still uncommon).
  DESIGN.md "The shared illness budget (the player's choice, 8 November 2026; made soft, 9 November 2026)" has all of it
  with the tables (old, new and the game's own side by side), and "Save size"; docs/balance-report.md the illness tables;
  README's paragraph and the crowding sentence; the Almanac's ailments page, *Sharing the game's own rate* (prose only,
  keywords unchanged).
  - What: **the hold is soft**: the game's next disease on a home that owes is held back three times in four
    (`HoldChance` 0.75, the roll in `TryHold`); otherwise it comes and the debt is let go as it lands (`GameCame`, the
    postfix; counted `cameAnyway`). **One debt at a time** stays (`MaxOwed` 1); 0.177.0's `GameTurn` (after a skip the
    game's own first) is gone. **After the game's own**, a firm pause of 8 days (`PauseDays`, `BudgetRoom.Waiting`), then
    a quarter of the chance coming back evenly to whole over four weeks (`EaseFrom`, `EaseDays`, `Eased`,
    `BudgetRoom.Easing`), not a flat 30 days. **More readily**: with the budget on, every new serious case of Rimfolk's
    (each cause of a colonist's day through `PersonFactor` and the diet's and after-cold's rolls, and the catching clock's
    serious one) is 2.75 times as likely at the usual disease interval (`Readiness`), leaning with the storyteller's
    interval by its power 1.5 (`ReadinessAt`: 1.5 times at Adventure story), since the budget's rules alone leave an
    average colony of six at a fifth or so. **Two at once, rarely**: someone already fighting a serious illness (one of
    Rimfolk's, anything a `DiseaseHuman` incident gives, or another lethal immunizable illness such as a wound infection:
    `IllnessBudget.IsSeriousIllness`) gets a new one of Rimfolk's at a quarter of the chance (`OverlapFactor`), from
    their day, from a roommate (`SpreadFactor`) and on the catching clock (`Spare`: someone well takes the place). The
    game's own diseases pick as before. Unchanged: everyday ailments, frailty, dirty wounds, what counts as the game's
    disease, the news lines (the held-back line is said only when the hold happened), the setting (on by default).
    Words: the letter no longer says the case takes the place of one of the game's own ("the next of them will most
    likely pass the colony by"); the setting's tip and note and the advisor's crowding line say "only a little more in
    all".
  - Code: `Ailments/IllnessBudgetMath.cs` (`HoldChance`, `PauseDays`, `EaseFrom`, `EaseDays`, `Readiness`,
    `ReadinessAt`, `IntervalLean`, `OverlapFactor`, `Overlap`, `MostInAll`, `Eased`, `Chance`, `Allows(roll)`,
    `Hold(roll)`, `GameCame(keep)`, `GapDays` for `WaitDays`, the targets `TargetShareMin/Max`, `TargetAbove`,
    `TargetTwoAtOnce`, `TargetTwoAtOnceRimfolk`; `MaxShare` and `BudgetRoom.GameTurn` gone), `IllnessBudget.cs`
    (`Allows` on the chance, `TryHold`'s roll, `Came` lets the debt go, `IsSeriousIllness`, `SeriouslyIll`,
    `SeriousFactor`, `SpreadFactor`, `Readiness`, `Spare`, the report), `AilmentTracker.cs` (`PersonFactor` and
    `SeriousFactor`, the diet's and after-cold's rolls, `Spread`, the clock's serious one), `IncidentWorker_Ailment`
    (`ActualVictims` spares the ill), `IllnessBudgetDebug` (says when one came all the same), `Rimfolk_IllnessBudget.xml`.
    Balance: `Sim.cs` plays the game's own diseases on the colonists (`Rates.GameDiseaseKinds`, a rough model: who and
    for how long, own draws) and counts two at once by which came on which; the budget's own draws (`budgetRng`) so the
    game's own come at the same hours on and off; the catching clocks and the land's serious ones lean with
    `--interval` as in the game; `IllnessSim.cs` prints the new columns and the table of two at once.

    the pause and the easing step by step, the readiness and its lean, the overlap factor, 4,000 years played out at five
    rates of demand, the seams in the code, the words never promising a place, and the balance report's two tables read
    against the targets).
  - Saved: `IllnessLedger.cameAnyway` (an int, "cameAnyway"); a 0.177.0 ledger loads it as none, an older save has no
    ledgers and owes nothing. `Tools/save_estimate.py` notes it in the budget's model.
  - Balance (600 colony-years a case, temperate forest; the game's own / 0.177.0 / now / no budget, in all a

    neglected 1.22 / 1.20 / 1.42 / 2.33; 12 colonists 1.25 / 1.25 / 1.36 / 1.54, 1.25 / 1.25 / 1.39 / 1.89, 1.16 / 1.16

    44%, 62% (12), where 0.177.0 had 8% to 32%; at Adventure story 0.84 to 0.92 kept well or fairly against the game's

    Rimfolk's 0.02 at most.
  - Riskiest (none of it could be run here): the readiness makes Rimfolk's serious illnesses come more often with the
    setting on than off in a well-run colony (0.31 against 0.19 for six), while fewer come in all; the Almanac's
    per-cause chances are those with it off (its budget section says so). `IsSeriousIllness` counts any lethal
    immunizable hediff and every `DiseaseHuman` incident's hediff (mods' included), so a mod's mild disease filed there
    counts as serious for the overlap. Pneumonia after the flu is a quarter as likely while the flu runs. The game's
    deadly diseases fall to 0.5 to 0.67 a colony-year (from about 0.8) as Rimfolk's take their turns; Rimfolk's can
    kill too, and the simulator counts no deaths. The victims and durations of the game's own in the simulator are a
    rough model, so the two-at-once numbers are a guide. A neglected colony of twelve sits a little over the quarter
    (+26% to +28%), from debts that lapse.

  - What: **the frame** (`UI/WindowFrame.cs`, rules in `UI/WindowFrameMath.cs`): a drawn title bar (icon, title, the
    window's tools, large, close), dragged by it, sized from every edge (6 in) and corner (16 along), down to the
    window's least, never off the screen; large (about 92% of the screen, above the bottom bar for the region window)
    with the button or a double-click on the title, and back; each window's place kept in the settings by its key
    (`windowPlaces`, "Region=x;y;w;h", ";L;" with the way back when large), fitted to the screen it opens on and
    refitted when the resolution or interface scale changes. The mouse is followed from the window's `WindowOnGUI` by
    polling (`Input.GetMouseButton(0)`, `UI.MousePositionOnUIInverted`). `FramedWindow` wires it to a plain window
    (margin 0, no game background, the contents in a group at zero). **The region window floats** (`UI/Window_Region.cs`):
    a plain window of the interface layer, opened by the region button's new worker (`MainButtonWorker_Region`), left
    open by a click on the map or a selection, the tab (`MainTabWindow_World`) only with the setting off. The choice:
    a main tab could have been dragged (only `SetInitialSizeAndPosition` anchors it), but the game closes a main tab on
    any map click (`MainTabsRoot.HandleLowPriorityShortcuts`) and on any selection (the selector opens the inspect pane),
    so a window moved aside to see the map would close the moment the map is used. Both draw the same contents
    (`MainTabWindow_World.DrawRegion`); `Pages.Showing`, `Show`, `Close`, `OpenOrClose`, `OpenOrCloseSection` and the new
    `LeaveForMap` know it; opening another of the four closes it (`RimfolkTabWindow.PreOpen`) and it closes another of
    Rimfolk's tabs, as the corner turns pages; the corner is in its title bar. **The kit** (`UI/UiKitSkin.cs`, shapes in
    `UI/SkinMath.cs`): rounded fills, edges, tab tops, corner masks (radii 4, 6, 8, 10) and a soft shadow made once at
    load, drawn as 9-slices; `Button` (normal, primary, quiet), `IconPlate`, `TextField`, `SearchField` (the game's quick
    search), `Toggle`, `OwnTab`, `RowLit`, `RowHover`, `OwnCard`, `CornerMask`, and the scrollbars' styles swapped while a
    framed window draws. The tokens are properties now, the game's value or the mockup's (`UiKit.BeginOwn`/`EndOwn` round
    a framed window's contents): Warm the mockup's blue, Sour its orange, Gold its amber; every text colour 4.5:1 or more
    on the window, a panel and a card. The kit's components (cards, chips, filter chips, modes, the lens bar, the view
    header's modes and "?", meters, the count badge, icon buttons, acts) draw rounded in the look and exactly as before
    in the game's. **Applied**: the region window (own tabs `WindowTabs.DrawOwn` on a rounded panel; the map's corners
    rounded with a mask, its zoom on plates; rows lit with the accent's edge; Peoples' search one field; the drawer a
    rounded card; the History filters, the journey's, the camp's and the faces' buttons the kit's) and the trade window
    (a `FramedWindow` "Trade", least 980 by 560: the title in the title bar, the search, chips and the switch the kit's,
    numbers right-aligned in the look, the side and the silver box raised cards, Accept primary, Reset quiet; its chips'
    words made once a trade now). Wider windows show more: Here and away and Faces in two columns from 1100
    (`RegionViewsMath.Columns`), Peoples' list 380 from a view of 1400, its acts in three columns from a page of 1180.

- 0.177.0, the shared illness budget (8 November 2026, the player's choice: they asked whether the game's own rate of health
  problems still holds or Rimfolk's illnesses stack on it, "since i lost several colonists to illness and seem to lose
  two more", and of three changes offered took one, "just the shared illness budget please"; frailty, dirty wounds and
  the everyday ailments stay as they were). Not released: no version, no What's new round, About.xml and CHANGELOG
  untouched (the lead does that at the merge). DESIGN.md "The shared illness budget" (under "Harm from everyday life",
  after the ailments of the land) has all of it with the balance numbers, and "Save size"; README's paragraph after the
  serious illnesses, the crowding sentence and the settings summary; the Almanac's ailments and illnesses page (a new
  section, *Sharing the game's own rate*, and the crowding and settings paragraphs; prose only, keywords unchanged).
  - What: Rimfolk's serious illnesses and the game's own diseases draw on one clock. Each serious case of Rimfolk's
    that starts on a home (not one passed on) owes a skip: the game's next human disease the storyteller aims there is
    held back. Once the game's own has come, Rimfolk's wait 30 days there; one debt at a time, and after a skip the
    game's own comes before Rimfolk takes another, so Rimfolk takes at most about a third of the cases on a temperate
    map (two fifths at Adventure story). Crowding still makes Rimfolk's catching kinds likelier, which only shifts the
    mix. Counts: the game's `DiseaseHuman` incidents sent by the storyteller to a home, not forced, not a quest's. Left
    alone: Rimfolk's own catching ailments, quests' and scripted outbreaks, forced ones, animal diseases, mods' sicknesses
    filed elsewhere, caravans, food poisoning, wound infections, the sickly trait's illness, the harm service's
    sicknesses. Shown: a news line when a disease is held back ("The council's records: the game's own flu passed the
    colony by this time; Rimfolk's tuberculosis, which Ana came down with, took its place.") or a case put off (one a
    home in 30 days, naming who was spared), a line in the serious illness's letter for a case the budget counted, and
    the advisor's sickness line saying crowding shifts the mix, with the last record.
  - Code: `Ailments/IllnessBudgetMath.cs` (pure, linked in Tests.csproj and Balance.csproj: `BudgetFiring`, `BudgetRoom`,
    `IllnessBudgetBook`, `Which`, `GameMeanDays`, `KeepDays`, `MaxShare`, `Owe`, `Hold`, `GameCame`, `Room`, `Prune`),
    `IllnessBudgetTests` ("illness budget: ", which incidents count, the game's rate, the debt, the cap, the reset,
    expiry, 4,000 years played out at four rates of demand with and without, the hook, the setting, the save, the
    words, the docs). `Ailments/IllnessBudget.cs`: `IllnessLedger`, `IllnessBudget` (`Allows`, `Owe`, `TryHold`, `Came`, the lines,
    `Report`), `Patch_IllnessBudget` (prefix and postfix on `Storyteller.TryFire`); `Ailments/IllnessBudgetDebug.cs`. Wired in
    `AilmentTracker` (`CanGet`, `Give`, `TryCatching`, `SeriousLetter`, `Ledger`, `PruneBudget`, saving),
    `IncidentWorker_Ailment` (the debt, the letter line) and `AdvisorWorker_SicknessRisk`. Keyed
    `Rimfolk_IllnessBudget.xml`. Balance: `Tools/Balance/IllnessSim.cs` (`--illness`, `--interval`, `--years`); the
    colony-year sim now keeps the colony's own room for a serious illness, crowding on the catching clock
    (`Rates.Style.barracks`, `kitchen`) and the game's own diseases on their own draws (`Rates.GameDiseaseMtbDays`), and
    `Colony.MeasuredYears` (1 for the report).
  - Settings: `illnessBudget` ("Serious illness shares the game's own rate", How hard, under Serious illnesses, on by
    default, needs serious illnesses and the deeper game hooks). Off: nothing owed (debts let go at the next daily look),
    as before.
  - Saved: `AilmentTracker.budget` ("illnessBudget": map uniqueID to `IllnessLedger`, deep): the debts and what each was
    for, the game's last disease and skip and what it paid, the last put-off, counts, the last record line; gone with the
    home or once all of it is older than a debt is kept. An older save has none and owes nothing. `Tools/save_estimate.py`
    models `budget`, `owed` and `owedFor`.
  - Balance (600 colony-years a case, temperate forest, Strive to survive): serious illness in all 1.18 to 1.25 a
    colony-year with the budget, the game's own alone 1.16 to 1.25 on the same seeds, 1.36 to 2.56 without it (16% to
    120% more); Rimfolk's own 0.19 to 0.10 well run, 1.05 to 0.34 neglected (6 colonists), its share 8% to 32% against a
    cap of 35%; the game's deadly ones 0.81 to 0.76 and 0.80 to 0.56. At Adventure story 0.74 to 0.85 with, 0.97 to 2.17
    without. DESIGN.md and docs/balance-report.md have the tables.
  - Riskiest (none of it could be run here): the hook on `Storyteller.TryFire`, the fourth prefix there (the others
    hold raids and the sky's conditions, never a disease; this one leaves a firing another prefix held, through
    `__runOriginal`, and pays no debt for it). ApiDiff finds it unchanged in 1.7. A storyteller mod that fires diseases
    another way would bypass the hold: debts would then lapse after two to five years, and Rimfolk's be capped by the
    one-at-a-time rule only;
    `StorytellerSends` looks only for `StorytellerCompProperties_Disease`, so a modded storyteller sending diseases
    through another part keeps debts the two-year minimum; the news lines' wording in real play (the game's disease is
    named by its `diseaseIncident.label`, a mod's may read oddly); a put-off case's line names who was spared, so it shows
    a roll the player never saw before; with the budget on, a well-run colony sees about half as many of Rimfolk's serious
    illnesses as before (the 30-day wait after the game's own), which is the point but may feel like Rimfolk's went quiet.

    written by a colonist and carried as letters are (mailbag, post, rider, relay, chain, call, go-between); their answer
    by their regard and their ways (`DealingMath.Chance`: base, regard 0.004 and goodwill 0.003 a point, their calling,
    the Empire's pride; 0.05 to 0.95), and it plays out once the answer is in. A supply contract (the colony's surplus or
    their goods by age, four seasons, porters at the gate both ways, two missed in a row break it); relief for a town in
    hard times (medicine, meals or raw food fetched by their porters; fortune +8, goodwill +6, `hardship`); a fair day (their
    caravan and three to six of their folk at an errand's pace, `Arrivals.Visit`, on the morning of a calendar gathering
    day, else six days on), friendship declared (+8 goodwill,

  they are closer. these thoughts must be applied to all such kinds of events"). Cause: `CampAnswers.Pay`/`Carry` and
  every carry to a camp (`DilemmaEffect_CarryOut` to `PlaySpot.Camp`) walked to the camp's fire wherever it stood. Fix:
  `Camps/CampMeet.cs` and `CampMeetMath.cs` (pure, linked): a camp whose fire is over 35 cells from the gate sends its
  person nearest the gate there (Goto at `Pace.Errand`, then a two-hour wait; kept for the session only), the carry
  waits ("CC_Play_Why_CampComing") and is handed over at the gate; a camper already within 9 cells of it takes it (the
  woodcutter with the bought wood). `PlayGroups` asks it before walking to the fire; `DilemmaImpact.Spot` words such a
  camp's spot "the gate, where one of the camp meets them". Tests in `FieldReportTests`. The woodcutters' own felling
  stays round their camp; the wood the colony buys already comes to the gate. To try: a camp far across the map, buy
  their wood or send a supper: a camper walks to the gate, the colonist meets them there.

  including the earlier couriers, seem to walk only quite slowly on the map, never as fast as my colonists move"). Cause:
  42 of Rimfolk's errands and exits used the game's `LocomotionUrgency.Walk` (half the ordinary pace), and every lord's
  `LordToil_Travel` walks at the travel duty's default, also Walk. Fix: `Source/ColonyCouncil/Pace.cs` (`Pace.Errand` =
  Jog, `LordToil_TravelOnErrand` setting its duties' locomotion), used by couriers, the post, the diplomacy parties,
  wards, visitors, camps' arrivals and leavings, strangers and missions leaving, the freed and ransomed. Kept slower on
  purpose (DESIGN.md "How fast Rimfolk's people go"): camp wandering, stall browsing, herds, packs and pets, play-out
  groups, carrying someone, the banished, the dawn and night walks. Test: `FieldReportTests` (the pace, and no Walk or
  plain travel toil in the couriers', post's, envoys', parties', visitors' and camps' files). To try: a courier or the
  post rider coming in keeps pace with a colonist walking beside it.

  the player: "this all sounds really good! visitors and other random characters should perhaps also be able to take
  letters when going their direction", with their addition the same day: "i should also have some sort of diplomatic

  DESIGN.md "The post: letters that travel with someone" has all of it (who carries, the way, the post by age, the rider,
  mail in, the console, writing, the range, what moved and what stayed, old saves); README two paragraphs after
  "Letters to the neighbours arrive in days" and the settings summary; the Almanac's neighbours page two sections (*The

  (keywords unchanged); the design doc's step 1 marked built.
  - What: a letter written goes in the mailbag at the gate (`Rimfolk_Mailbag`, a Misc spot; none placed, the gate cell),
    its pane listing each letter and how it is likely to leave. Whoever leaves the map going its way takes it: any lord of
    a people at peace whose job goes about the road (traders, visitors and Hospitality's guests, a camp, pilgrims,
    travellers, messengers and envoys) turning to leave, a lone outsider walking off, the colony's own caravan forming;
    one of them walks to the mailbag for it. On their way: their own people's towns, a town on the road to their
    destination, or within 60 degrees of the way they leave. A regular post by the colony's and its neighbours' shared
    age (none tribal, a rider every 7 to 14 days medieval, a mail run 3 to 7 industrial, a shuttle 2 to 4 spacer by drop
    pod; the pace a setting), mounted on their people's caravan beasts or a horse, with Giddy-Up's "Mount" job by name,
    else leading it. The colony's own rider (the letter's window or the mailbag's button) rides out as a caravan of one
    with a colony animal big enough to ride and brings the answer home. Answers of words only and the world's carried
    letters (a town's, the envoy's and the ward's from abroad) wait for whoever comes in from their way and open when set
    down at the mailbag; a messenger only after half a day (urgent), three days (business), eight or twelve (ordinary).
    Writing takes someone who can read (`BookUtility.CanReadEver`); a tribe gives spoken messages at the gate. The comms
    console to peoples with radio (industrial on, or within 30 tiles of a Signal Line town, by its def's name). The range
    until radio: the world's own travel time (the game's path and `CaravanArrivalTimeEstimator`: terrain, roads, rivers, season, snow) at the
    carrier's means, five days by runners, seven riders, nine vehicles, half again with a mast, none for shuttles; far
    towns by relay through a nearer town on good terms, out-of-reach towns only with someone going there. Each town's
    card says how to reach them and roughly how soon; the region map rings far (amber) and out-of-reach (grey) towns.
  - Moved to the outbox: every letter by hand of `NeighbourLetters` (the diplomacy purposes too), words-only answers,

- 0.169.0, peoples whose age changes (8 November 2026, the first piece of `docs/design/peoples-third.md`, approved by the player:
  "also changing over time: do both", "our older factions should also be able to grow and develop over time to reach
  higher research levels"). Not released: no version, no What's new round, About.xml and CHANGELOG untouched. DESIGN.md
  "Peoples whose age changes" has all of it (the rule, each people's pace and limit, the simulation's numbers, what
  follows, where the game's own tech level couldn't follow); README a paragraph after the peoples; the Almanac's page on
  the road league, the hospitallers and the herders a section *Their age over the years* (prose only, keywords unchanged);
  `peoples-third.md` step 1 marked built.
  - What: each of Rimfolk's peoples (and each that arose in their ways) is looked at once a season and moves toward the
    next age at its ways' pace (`agePace`, years an age, and `ageLimit` in every def with a line of why: the society 6.5,
    the Conclave and the league 7, the guild 8, the Wheel 10, the Banner 11, the Circuit 12, the enclave 8 at spacer
    already, the hospitallers 12 to industrial, the Wardens and the river folk 13, the pilgrims 16, the Bell 17, the
    herders 20 to industrial, the Mossborn 24 to medieval), quickened by the colony's trade (twice at 5000 silver a year),
    gifts of books, techprints, components and tools, theirs who learned at the colony and their masters who taught the
    colony's people, and an alliance or pact (three times at most); cut off (no trade with anyone for years, towns
    burned, at war with most of the world: two of the three) it falls back an age in five to ten years, never more than
    one below where it began. The Sunken Vault's way (`ageDeclines`, `ageDeclineYears`): built and tested, no people has it
    yet. A letter for each change in their own voice (their leader's words by calling), their card and the region's page
    of peoples show the age and heading with why. Their next pawns are dressed and armed for the age (new sets for nine
    of the first seven peoples' fighting kinds; and the every-age pass, `AgeArms.ToAge`: nothing of a later age, a
    fighter's bow becomes a gun of the age), their camps' kits, words, messengers, ransoms, travel and town stores follow
    (`Peoples.TechOf` in some 60 of Rimfolk's reads), and their traders' caps move with the age. The numbers (400 worlds):
    by themselves 0 of 15 rise in 5 years and 4.8 in 10; a typical game 2.0 in 5, 4.1 in 7.5, 6.1 in 10, the guild two
    ages in half the worlds; all the colony's help takes the guild from medieval to spacer within 10 years in every world.
  - Code: `Peoples/PeopleAgesMath.cs` (pure, linked in Tests.csproj; `PeopleAgesTests`, "peoples' ages: ", 360 checks:
    the rule, the defs, the simulation, every kind of the fifteen in every age it can reach against the player's
    catalogue, the seams), `PeopleAges.cs` (the record and book, the look from `RegionBook.Daily`, what the rule reads),
    `PeopleAgeWords.cs` (the letter, the history's `world:age`, the card and page line), `PeopleAgePatches.cs`
    (`Patch_PeopleAgeGiftThing` on `FactionGiftUtility.GiveGiftInternal`, `Patch_PeopleAgeGiftTraded` and
    `Patch_PeopleAgeGiftPods` on the two `GiveGift`s, `Patch_PeopleAgeStock` on `ThingSetMaker_TraderStock.Generate`),
    `PeopleAgesDebug.cs`; `Peoples.AgeOf` reads the record, `Peoples.BeganIn` and `TechOf` new; `PeopleGifts.cs` (kit-only
    sets, a set's arms of the age, `AgeArms.ToAge`, genes only from the industrial age); two new deeds in
    `FactionMemory.Kinds` (`gaveLearning`, `learnedHere`, noted by `MemoryHooks.MissionEnded` for the two hosted
    learners); Keyed `Rimfolk_PeopleAges.xml`. Tests changed only where they read code that now reads the age
    (PeoplesTests' no-book rule, WorldMechanicsTests' `Ages.Of`, RansomTests' pod, PeoplesGearTests' gifted kinds).
  - Settings: `peopleAges` ("Peoples' ages change", the region's toggles, on). Saved: `PeopleAgeBook.ages` (one record a
    people, `MaxRecords` 40, modelled in `save_estimate.py`).
  - Where the game couldn't follow (its own methods read the def's field): what traders buy, the stuff of stock and of the
    game's own gear, raids' drop pods, the game's own base where a plan doesn't fit, quests by tech level. Town plans are
    the same in every age.
  - Riskiest: the finalizer that puts a trader's caps back (a stock generator shared by every trader of that kind, changed
    only while one stock is made); `GiveGiftInternal` by name (both gift paths are believed to go through it: a pod's gift
    that doesn't is simply not counted); trade matched to a people by the trade record's names (its own and its towns',

  - Try in the game (dev mode; none of it could be run here): 1. "Peoples: every people's age and progress (log)": each

    2. Trade with a people (sell and buy a few thousand silver) and gift it books or components: the log's trade and
    gifts rise, its card and the region's Peoples page read "rising: trades with you, has your gifts of learning", and
    the World page's memory lists "gave them books and components". 3. "Peoples: a people up an age now (testing)..." on

    sworn guards in flak with guns, lay archers with rifles, their caravan's clothes and weapons for sale of the industrial age; one
    of their camps builds with the industrial kit. 4. "a people down an age now" on the league: a medieval league, no guns

- 0.168.1, a pet bitten on the hunt still eats (8 November 2026, the player's bug report: "my pet hunted for food, got
  slightly injured in the fight, and then started walking back to base without eating"). Cause: the hunts' watch
  (`PetHunts.Watch`) ended a chase for any reason that bars starting one, and a fresh bite wants tending
  (`ShouldSeekMedicalRest`, "sick") while prey that turns on its hunter raises the map's danger ("danger"), so the chase
  was broken off before the kill and the pet went to bed hungry. Fix: `HuntMath.StopChase` (pure, tested in `HuntTests`),
  the chase's own rule: the player's word, a call to follow, a group, a mental state, downed, unable, under 0.35 of its
  health (`ChaseMinHealth`), bleeding out within a day (`ChaseBleedTicks`), or danger besides the prey itself
  (`PetHunts.OtherDanger`: the map's hostile targets other than the prey). Starting a hunt is unchanged (`WhyNot`).
  DESIGN.md (pets that hunt, Harm) and the Almanac's animals page (prose) say so. To try: a hungry dog with nothing it may
  eat in its area, a hare or a fox near; let it be bitten and see it keep on, kill and eat before going to rest.
- 0.168.0, bed rest only when it makes sense (8 November 2026, the player's explicit request: "when does a pawn ... rest with an
  ailment or injury or illness, and when can the pawn still work ... I just don't want ... if someone has a bit of a
  sunburn that they just stay in bed all day ... they have a negative impact normally, but they don't keep a pawn
  bedridden unless it also kind of makes sense ... review our ailments and perhaps also the one already in game", and
  their word on the first draft: "pawns should only bed rest if it's a serious condition, they have strong pain, they are
  bleeding etc., not for 'minor' problems. perhaps they sleep a bit more, but not all day long"). Not released: no
  version, no What's new round, About.xml and CHANGELOG untouched. DESIGN.md "Bed rest only when it makes sense" (how the
  game decides, the rule's table, who it leaves alone, where it hooks in, the line, Rimfolk's 85 ailments one by one,
  the game's and the mods' conditions by family, the other medical mods); README "Recovery, doctors and midwives" a
  paragraph, the settings summary and "Optional mods"; the Almanac's hospital beds page a section (*Who rests in bed
  (Rimfolk)*) and its ailments page a paragraph in *Medicine, rest and recovery*, no keyword changed.
  - What: the game's `ShouldSeekMedicalRest` (any tended wound still healing, any catching illness not yet immune) is the
    rule's: bed rest only for a serious wound while it heals (medicine by what is treated's Serious), wounds that together
    bring strong pain (15%, the game's line past "minor pain") or leave a leg or the hands poor (70%, the health tab's
    "poor"), an illness that can kill until immune, a stage of any illness in strong pain or 30% or more off
    consciousness, moving or breathing, Rimfolk's ailments from their def's `restFrom`, and the game's urgent cases (down,
    surgery, labor, something to tend; small things to tend, not losing blood, wait at work while no doctor is free). The
    game's and mods' conditions only lose rest the game gave; Rimfolk's follow the rule alone. Babies, non-flesh and
    mutants, the player's "rest until healed", the rest when ill decree, another mod's own reason and Smart Medicine's
    "Bed rest" box unticked stay as the game or the player has them. A stage they work through that tires them has them
    sleep a little more (its `restFallFactor`), at most half as fast again (about nine hours, never all day).
  - Code: `Health/BedRestMath.cs` (pure, linked in Tests.csproj; `BedRestTests`, "bed rest: ", 387 checks: the
    thresholds, wounds by `MedicineChoiceMath.Judge`, the game's and mods' illness families, the urgent cases, orders, the
    decree, another mod's reason, sleeping more, every stage of all 85 of Rimfolk's ailments from their defs, the seams),
    `Health/BedRest.cs` (the facts, a per-pawn cache a tick and a second, `GameRest`, the line, the report, `Explain`),
    `Health/BedRestPatches.cs` (`Patch_BedRest` postfix on `HealthAIUtility.ShouldSeekMedicalRest`;
    `Patch_BedRestHealedNotice` transpiler on `Pawn_HealthTracker.HealthTickInterval` sending the "fully healed" notice's
    one call to the game's own answer, or the rule stays off; `Patch_BedRestOrder` prefix and finalizer on
    `Building_Bed.GetBedRestFloatMenuOption`; `Patch_BedRestTooltip` on `Hediff.GetTooltip` after the medicine line;
    `Patch_BedRestReport` on `JobDriver_LayDown.GetReport`), `Health/BedRestDebug.cs`, Keyed `Rimfolk_BedRest.xml`,
    `SmartMedicineBridge.OffBedRest` (its `ignoredHediffs`). The two HediffSet checks are left alone: one also decides
    whether tended wounds heal, the other a caravan's bedrolls. Defs: `restFrom` on `HediffCompProperties_Ailment`
    (checked at load) for fourteen serious illnesses (appendicitis 0.25; anthrax, bird fever, glassblood, hive fever, swamp
    fever, tetanus, typhus, valley fever 0.3; rabies 0.5, shingles 0.5, measles 0.6, tuberculosis 0.6, scurvy 0.75); a
    modest `restFallFactor` (1.05 to 1.2) on sixteen stages worked through (the colds' first stage, the stomach bug's
    vomiting, the sprain, the strained and torn back, rabbit fever, and six serious illnesses' first stage). No other
    downside added: every ailment keeps its pain, capacities and mood (the table in DESIGN.md).
  - Settings: `restByNeed` ("Bed rest only when it makes sense", What's on, people's lives, after medicine by what is
    treated, on, needs the deeper hooks). Nothing saved; no Sched slot; no letters or messages.
  - Riskiest: every reader of `ShouldSeekMedicalRest` follows the rule (a medical bed no longer valid for someone the rule
    keeps working, so they get up after being tended; fed and visited only when resting; the hospital bed at night); the
    transpiler on the health tick (by the call, not by IL around it; not found, the rule is off with a warning); the
    "doctor free" look (the game's `AnyAvailableDoctorFor`) can have someone with a sunburn get up when the doctors go
    to sleep and lie down again in the morning; Move the Patient's own "Transfer to bed" of someone the rule keeps working
    leaves them in a bed they get up from, as the game does for the healthy; Smart Medicine's box read by name; Rimfolk's
    serious illnesses' early stages now worked through rather than rested (immunity about a fifth slower for those days;
    the tests' survival runs never counted bed); Hospitality's guests and other mods that ask the game's question.
  - Try in the game (dev mode; none of it could be run here): 1. Debug actions, Rimfolk, "Bed rest: a test patient (a head
    cold, a sunburn, a tended cut and bruise)...": the colonist lies down to have the sunburn tended (a doctor free), then
    gets up and works; the health tab's tooltips say "Keeps working, and sleeps a little more." (the cold), "Keeps working,
    lying down only to be tended." (the sunburn before tending), "Keeps working." (the cut, the bruise). Without the
    setting (or with "Use medical bed") they stay in bed. 2. Add the flu (the game's Add hediff): they go to bed, the
    flu's line says "Rests in bed: an illness that can kill, and bed helps the body fight it.", the cold's "Keeps working
    with this alone, but is in bed now for the flu.", and the inspect pane "resting: flu.". 3. After a raid: a gunshot in
    the torso rests until it heals ("Rests in bed until it heals: a wound that bleeds heavily."), a colonist with only
    bruises and a scratch gets up once tended; several cuts with 15% pain rest. 4. "Bed rest: why each one rests or works
    (log)...": each condition's verdict, whether the game counts it, the wounds' pain, moving and manipulation. 5. The
    "fully healed" message comes once when the last wound closes, not every ten seconds. 6. Enact the council's rest when
    ill decree: the cold keeps them in bed again ("Rests in bed: the council's decree to rest when ill."). 7. With Smart
    Medicine: right-click the flu, untick "Bed rest": they get up, and the line says so. 8. A colonist with tuberculosis
    under treatment works through it (consumption: slower, sleeping more) and goes to bed only if it reaches wasting.
    9. "Rimfolk: check myself": the five Patch_BedRest classes applied.
