    2. The colonist's button "Show the wrong-style things": the chairs and table are selected; from another room or with
       the camera elsewhere, the camera goes to the first. Somewhere with nothing against them: the rejection message.
    3. Select a chair: its inspect text says "Against ...'s style: " and the colonist's name.
    4. Make the colonist's ideoligion the main one (or pick a style for it the main one shares): the fix line says to build
       them again. A small room under 10 cells: the threshold is its cell count.
    5. "Wrong-style things: the count around a colonist (log)...": the groups, Rimfolk's total and the game's own sum from
       the same cell (`GetStyleDominanceFromCellsCenteredOn`): the two should agree. Classic mode or the setting off:
       nothing of it shows.
- 0.166.0, a bleeding animal's body taken when it dies (8 November 2026, the player's explicit request: "if i see a
  wild animal is bleeding out, can i give a command to haul it's corpse once it's dead? not to hunt it, in case it's a
  strong one, but just to wait for it to die. if the animal recovers from bleeind comehow, this job shouild be
  cancelled."). Not released: no version, no What's new round, About.xml and CHANGELOG untouched (the lead numbers and
  releases it at the merge). DESIGN.md "A bleeding animal's body taken when it dies" (and the 193 row of "Ticking");
  README "The colony's animals" a paragraph; the Almanac's colony's animals page a section (*Waiting for a bleeding animal
  to die*) and a phrase in *Who hunts, and what*, no keyword changed.
  - What: the button "Take the body when it dies" on a living, spawned, bleeding animal that isn't the colony's (wild or
    another people's). It puts Rimfolk's designation `Rimfolk_TakeBodyWhenDead` on it (the game's haul icon, drawn over
    the animal, saved with the map, taken off by the game's Cancel), in place of a hunting or taming order. Nothing is done
    while it lives; the colony's pets leave it out of their prey. When it dies, however it dies, its body is unforbidden
    and given the game's own `Haul` order (unless it already lies in storage); with no storage on the map that takes it,
    one message (the body the look target). Dropped on its own, one message naming the animal and why, when it stops
    bleeding (aged out, tended, healed), is tamed, joins the colony or leaves the map; dropped without a word when the
    player cancels or replaces it, or the setting or hooks are off. The tooltip: what it does, the bleeding rate, and the
    outlook by the game's rules (it bleeds to death in about the health tab's figure, or it shouldn't: its wounds stop on
    their own in so long, or it makes its blood up under 10% a day).
  - Code: `Animals/BodyWhenItDiesMath.cs` (pure, linked in Tests.csproj; `BodyWhenItDiesTests`, "the body when it dies: ",
    71 checks: the button, `Judge` and the messages, `Outlook` against hand-worked cases, the haul order, the seams),
    `Animals/BodyWhenItDies.cs` (the DefOf, the button and its tooltip, `Put`, `MarkedMap`/`Died` for the kill, `Rare`),
    `Animals/BodyWhenItDiesPatches.cs` (`Patch_BodyWhenItDiesKill`, a prefix and postfix on `Pawn.Kill`: the game removes
    every order on the animal in `Thing.Destroy`, after the body is placed, so the prefix reads the mark and the postfix
    acts once `Dead`; `Patch_BodyWhenItDiesGizmo` on `Pawn.GetGizmos`), `Animals/BodyWhenItDiesDebug.cs`,
    `Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_BodyWhenItDies.xml`, Keyed `Rimfolk_BodyWhenItDies.xml`. One line each in `BeastBook.Rare` (the
    short pass, every 250 ticks: no Sched slot), `PetHunts.PreyOf` and `HuntMath.WhyNotPrey` (`markedForBody`).
  - Settings: `bodyWhenItDies` ("Take a bleeding animal's body when it dies", What's on, Strangers and creatures, on, under
    the deeper hooks: an indented row, so the setups that switch parts off leave it be). Saved: nothing new (the designation is the game's; which marked animals were
    wild is session memory, filled again from the marks after a load).
  - Riskiest: the kill's prefix and postfix (another mod that stops or reworks a death: the postfix acts only once the
    animal is `Dead` and its body spawned); taming read from the faction after the game's `SetFaction` took the order off
    (a wild animal that another people takes over is dropped silently as "cancelled"); the storage check without a carrier
    (`TryFindBestBetterStorageFor(corpse, null, ...)`, so reachability isn't checked: storage behind a wall counts as
    storage); the outlook leaves out other causes of death (an infection, a predator) and wounds of other mods that bleed
    (counted as never closing by age).
  - Try in the game (dev mode, Debug actions, Rimfolk, "Body when it dies: ..."; none of it could be run here):
    1. "a deep cut on an animal (bleeds out)..." on a wild boar: it bleeds (the message says the rate and when it dies).
       Select it: the button "Take the body when it dies", its tooltip with "At this rate it bleeds to death in about ...",
       the same figure as its health tab. Press it: the haul icon over it, the game's Cancel button on it instead.
    2. Wait (or the game's Kill tool): the body is unforbidden with the haul icon, and a hauler takes it to a stockpile that
       allows corpses. With no such stockpile: one message, "... has died, but no storage on the map takes its body ...".
    3. Mark another bleeding animal, then "tend an animal's wounds (stops the bleeding)...": within 250 ticks the mark is
       gone and "... has stopped bleeding, so the order to take its body is cancelled.". The same with "age an animal's
       wounds past bleeding..."; tame one (the game's Tame order, or the dev tame tool): "... has been tamed ..."; one that
       walks off the map: "... has left the map ...".
    4. "a light cut on an animal (lives)...": the tooltip says it shouldn't bleed to death and when its wounds close.
    5. Mark a boar a pet of the colony could hunt (Pets hunt for themselves): the pet leaves it alone. Mark one already
       marked for hunting: the hunt order goes. The setting off: the button is gone, and marks left are dropped quietly.
    6. "the marked animals (log)": each with its rate, the health tab's figure, when it dies or that it lives, and when its
       wounds close. Save and load with a mark on: the mark is still there and still dropped as above.
- 0.165.0, Rimfolk's own trade window (7 and 8 November 2026, the player's request: "i still don't really like the new trade
  interface, i'm thinking more of a totally redone one by you, not an adjusted vanilla one. where I can see whether I'm
  buying/selling above/under market price, what are really good deals both ways, easier sorting & overview etc"; built
  without a proposal round). Not released: no version, no What's new round, About.xml and CHANGELOG untouched (the lead
  numbers and releases it at the merge). New: `Trade/TradeWindow.cs` (the opening, the switch both ways, the button
  back, `Patch_TradeWindowOpen` on `WindowStack.Add`), `Trade/Window_RimfolkTrade.cs` (the window), `Trade/TradeWindowMath.cs`
  (pure: the grades, the shares, the sort, the sums, the best deals, the columns that fit, the chips' rows, the scroll to
  a row, the kinds; linked in Tests.csproj), Keyed `Rimfolk_TradeWindow.xml`, `Tools/Tests/TradeWindowTests.cs` ("trade
  window: ", 510 checks). Changed: `TradeScreen.cs` (`Trading` counts Rimfolk's window; the readouts' lines and the
  basket's two states public for it; `Fill`/`Clear` take a null screen; the row marks stand down while Rimfolk's window
  draws the game's row icons; the button back beside the game's sort menus in `Patch_TradeFoot`), `TradeAdvice.cs` (each
  note keeps its usual prices, `UsualPrices`, `GainAndLoss`, `UsualFor` for people and animals), the setting, DESIGN.md
  "The trade screen" (rewritten, the 0.150.0 bullets kept under "The game's screen and the advice"), README "The trade
  screen", the Almanac page *the trade screen* (three new sections, prose only, no keyword changed). Nothing saved.
  - Opening: the game's constructor sets the trade up (`TradeSession.SetupWith`), and every opener adds it with
    `WindowStack.Add` (a trader, visitor or Hospitality guest on the map by `JobDriver_TradeWithPawn`, a ship by comms, a
    caravan at a town, a caravan met on the road, pods at a town), so the prefix swaps the window and keeps the game's
    own `Dialog_Trade`. Only that exact class (a mod's subclass is left), only silver (a trade in favor keeps the game's
    screen), never gifts (gifts-only and gift mode stay the game's; "Give gifts" in the window goes there). "Game's
    screen" (top right) takes the window off and adds that same `Dialog_Trade`, let through once; the counts are the
    deal's, so they stay. On the game's screen a 27-pixel button right of its sort menus (x 360, where it draws no search
    box) comes back, the game's screen taken off by `TryRemove` so its `Close` (a trader's quest) waits for the end.
  - The window: one table with sides (the colony's count and what they pay left of the game's own
    `DoCountAdjustInterface`, what they ask and their count right of it, as its arrows go), thirteen columns (name, kind,
    value, ours, they pay, count, they ask, theirs, deal, market and trend with VTE's history, mass, need), rows 36 high.
    Under each price its share of the market value (`BaseMarketValue`) and its side of the usual (the advice's), green 7%
    better for the colony, orange 7% worse. At 1920 every column fits with about 300 pixels of name beside a 300-pixel
    side; at 1280 the mass, kind, trend and market give way (`TradeWindowMath.Fit`, tested at both). Header clicks sort
    (again for the other way; the last sort kept for the session), a search, kind chips, "only in the deal"; on the right
    the best five sells and buys (a click scrolls to the row and lights it) and the deal's summary; at the foot Fill
    suggested, Clear suggested, Reset, Accept, Cancel, each side's silver now and after. A caravan's mass, speed and food
    are the game's strip at the top (its calculators, over every good). Accept: the game's question when the trader is
    short, then `TryExecute`; the game's own can't-pay check and message first, since `TryExecute` flashes a
    `Dialog_Trade` it looks up (there is none). On close a trader's quest is handed over; on opening, the game's word
    about an impaired negotiator. Any throw while drawing: logged once and the game's screen takes over.
  - Grades (`TradeWindowMath.Rate`): the price against the usual (a sale's price over it, a purchase's usual over the
    price), 0.05 a step for VTE's market reason (`TradeMarketMath.Hint`) and for the colony's record (better than its
    best of 15 days by 2%, or a tenth worse); great from 1.20 (the advice's good sale), good from 1.07, fair from 0.93,
    else poor; a purchase not marked worth buying, or a sale of what is short or all kept, held at fair. Bars and a word;
    people not graded. Example: steel worth 2.28 on VTE's market (20% up, 1.90 usual worth), a negotiator of +12%: they
    pay 1.53 (67% of value, +20% on the usual 1.28), at a 60-day high and above the colony's best 1.40 of the week:
    1.20 + 0.05 + 0.05 = 1.30, a great sell; they ask 2.81 (123%, +20% on the usual 2.34), 0.83, a poor buy.
  - Settings: What's on, Trade screen, *Rimfolk's own trade window* (`tradeWindow`, on, first in the section, deeper
    hooks). The game's screen's switches are as they were.
  - Riskiest: the `WindowStack.Add` swap (another mod that adds a `Dialog_Trade` and then looks it up with
    `WindowOfType<Dialog_Trade>` finds none while Rimfolk's window is open: the game itself only does so in
    `TryExecute`'s can't-pay branch, handled first); a mod that patches `Dialog_Trade`'s own drawing or `PostOpen` to set
    a trade up (none known: VTE draws nothing there, Trade Helper's panel is its drawing) does nothing in Rimfolk's
    window; the game's screen reopened as the same instance (its `PreOpen` and `PostOpen` run again; an impaired
    negotiator's message shows again at the switch); the caravan calculators and `CaravanUIUtility.DrawCaravanInfo`
    called directly; the count control's text field inside a scroll view that only draws the rows in sight (as the
    game's own screen does); the colours on dark and light themes (Rimfolk's UiKit). Hospitality's and Trade Helper's code
    isn't in the player's files (only Hospitality's defs, a trader kind for guests): what they do on a trade was read from
    those and Trade Helper's description, not their code.
  - Try in the game (none of it could be run here):
    1. A caravan or visitor at home: Rimfolk's window opens. Read a row of steel or wood: value, they pay with its share
       and its side of the usual, they ask the same; compare a price with the game's (Game's screen, its price
       tooltip), then come back with the button right of its sort menus and see the counts kept.
    2. Set counts with the arrows (Shift, Ctrl), type one, press the double arrows; check "Only in the deal" and the
       summary (sold, bought, net silver, against usual, by market value, food days); Fill suggested, Clear suggested,
       Reset.
    3. Click each column's header twice; type in the search; pick a kind chip; with a good hidden, click it in Best deals
       and see the filters clear and the row light.
    4. Sell more than the trader's silver and press Accept: the game's question; buy more than the colony's silver: the
       game's message, the silver at the foot lit. Trade, then open the next trade and see the record's step in a deal's
       tooltip.
    5. An orbital trader by comms with goods near a beacon (the bought goods come by pod); a caravan at a town (the game's
       strip at the top with mass and food after the trade); a caravan met on the road; a Hospitality guest.
    6. With VTE: the Market and Trend columns, a good at a 60-day high graded a step up, the impact line in the summary
       after setting a big sale. At 1280 by 720 (UI scale 1): the columns that give way, nothing overlapping.
    7. Give gifts (the game's gift mode); a trade with the Empire's tribute collector (the game's screen); the setting off
       (the game's screen, no button back); deeper hooks off (the same).
- 0.164.0, harm, part 7: tempers in the colony, visitors and outsiders, personal stories (7 and 8 November 2026, the last of the three
  batches of the review's remaining proposals after the player's "all suggestions please", on the shared budget so they add
  variety and not more hurts in all). With it **every one of the review's 94 proposals is built**. Not released: no version,
  no What's new round, About.xml and CHANGELOG untouched (the lead numbers and releases it at the merge); merged with main at
  0.163.0. Twenty-eight kinds (1.1.2, 1.3.1, 1.3.2, 1.5.1, 3.5.2, 3.7.1, 3.9.1, 3.9.2, 3.10.1, 3.13.1, 4.1.3, 4.7.3, 3.12.2;
  1.2.4, 2.2.2, 2.5.3, 2.6.2, 2.8.2, 2.8.3, 2.9.1, 2.9.2, 3.8.1, 3.13.2, 2.3.2, 2.3.3; 3.10.2, 3.10.3, 4.8.1) and three that
  hurt nobody of the colony, outside the budget (2.10.1 the nemesis's aim, 2.6.1 a neighbour's lost child, 2.7.1 their
  courier). `Harm/HarmSevenMath.cs` (the rates, `HarmSevenTests`, "harm seven: ", 966 checks; linked in Tests.csproj and
  Balance.csproj), `Harm/HarmSeven.cs` (the hub on the harm book's hour and slices, a moment set for later), `Tempers.cs`,
  `GateTroubles.cs` (with `DilemmaEffect_GamblerTurns` and an `Outsiders` partial: `HarmBrawl`, `Challenge`,
  `TakesChallenge`, `FistfightChance`), `Stories.cs`, `HarmSevenDebug.cs`; `Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_HarmSeven.xml` (the jobs
  `Rimfolk_PracticeWalk`, `Rimfolk_StoresSneak`, both `JobDriver_HarmWalk`), `Defs/FlavorPoolDefs/Rimfolk_HarmSeven_Lines.xml`
  (51 pools, in `ImmersionTests.SpokenPools`), Keyed `Rimfolk_HarmSeven.xml`, `Defs/ThoughtDefs/Rimfolk_Thoughts_HarmSeven.xml`
  (`Rimfolk_Harm_StartedTheFight`, an opinion only). DESIGN.md "Harm, part 7" (a table of the thirty-one) and "The rates"
  redone; README "Hurts from everyday life" three bullets; the Almanac's ailments page (prose only, no keyword changed);
  the review marks each built with what differs, and its Summary says it is complete.
  - Registry (`HarmKinds`, founding false, base rates from the model at 4000 runs): sitDown 0.021, speakerWords 0.0035,
    passedOver 0.0054, meetingBoils 0.0081, friendsStand 0.0145, saidToFace 0.020, wrongedOne 0.0043, toldByFriend 0.0056,
    loveRivals 0.0138, altarWords 0.0031, feastFists 0.0149, secondRound 0.0052, soldierNight 0.0023, openGates 0.018,
    gamblerTurns 0.0019, barberNick 0.0105, rankEnemy 0.0005, crowdFight 0.0018, pastFirstBlood 0.0003, letterChallenge
    0.0014, heirGrudge 0.0008, hatedTrader 0.0035, gateZeal 0.0026, hungryHands 0.0039, creekBrawl 0.0002, worstNight
    0.0021, firstSteps 0.0014, workingWrong 0.0058; each a system of its own in `Harm.SystemOn` (speakerWords only under
    demanding stakes, `s.Harsh`; the outsiders' fistfights with the deeper hooks; secondRound with Vanilla Brewing
    Expanded, `Tempers.BrewingLoaded`; workingWrong with A RimWorld of Magic, `Contests.MagicLoaded`). 100 kinds now; each
    passes at about 31% of its own rate. Most of part 7's kinds are fights, and a fight is two hurts the cap counts.
  - The thirty-one (rate, prevention; seen). Tempers: (1.1.2) the peacemaker's sit-down (`Offices.Mediate`), 1 in 10 at a
    rivalry of 70, nothing at 30, less with Social, half without a hot temper; not mended that time; the peacemaker steps
    between them and takes a punch 1 time in 3. (1.3.1) a broken promise under demanding stakes, bitter (doubtful or worse)
    and hot-tempered, a fifth: the walk to the speaker within the day, words by the age, talked down by the speaker's Social
    (a twentieth a level), else a fight. (1.3.2) passed over (the jealousy rule), the jealous or abrasive: for a week the
    first two meetings a sharp word, each at the game's insult chance for a pair at -20 (0.064); the peacemaker's word
    within two days settles it. (1.5.1) two rivals who both pitched and stayed, 1 meeting in 12, half with the peacemaker at
    the table, the chair's Social; the meeting's comment no longer says nobody is hurt over it. (3.5.2) any social fight at
    home, one look: a close friend (45 friendship or 60 opinion) within twelve cells, 1 in 6 runs over, a blow 1 time in 2,
    the two pulled apart (their fight ends; "to help" left out). (3.7.1) gossip run down to its subject's face, a hot
    temper, 1 in 10, the blows a moment after the words. (3.9.1) a secret that wronged the colony (`SecretDef.wrongsColony`
    on six: the stores thief, the borrowed cooking, the failed apprentice, the skimmed take, the mutiny, the caravan's dice)
    let slip: whoever heard it, 1 in 4 (half with the peacemaker), goes to the owner; never one confessed. (3.9.2) a
    confidence betrayed: 1 leak in 5 the keeper goes to the friend, blows half the time. (3.10.1) "a rival in love" leaving
    its rivals' stage, the words said within two hours, 1 in 4 a shove; the one they both like thinks less of the starter.
    (3.13.1) the one-faith decree (`DecreeHurt.OneFaith`, on its card): the first evening of its faith with a devout of
    another at home, 1 in 3 the devout comes to blows with its speaker. (4.1.3) a day's table quarrel (`SetbackTimes`) with
    drink in one of them, 1 in 4. (4.7.3) with Vanilla Brewing Expanded, two cups of alcohol in stock for each who drank:
    one toast in three pours a second round (the policy for joy, faith, never an addict); two rivals who both took it, 1 in
    4 within the hour; `ToastDrinks.cs` untouched (the hook is in `PlayOutLord`). (3.12.2) a nightmare that left a soldier's
    or outlaw's past shaken, a roommate asleep: 1 in 20 (seeded) the roommate's mildest bruise. Visitors: (1.2.4) the
    open-gates decree (`DecreeHurt.Gates`, on its card), its first visitors one roll, half (the warden half, on guard half):
    a thief to the stores (`Rimfolk_StoresSneak`; seen within fifteen cells, chased, the sack dropped, caught a fistfight
    half the time; unseen, off with a stack of up to ten of something cheap) or a beer of their own and a fight in the
    yard. (2.2.2) "let anyone play" (`DilemmaEffect_GamblerTurns` on both its outcomes, its sheet line): the evening's
    games, 1 in 6 a cheat caught, a hot-tempered loser's fistfight, the gambler sent on. (2.5.3) the barber, 1 cut in 30
    (twice under Artistic 6) a cut of 1 on the shoulder; a spacer people's barber never. (2.6.2) a dignitary at home, 1 in 6
    a hothead of their own people at the gate; their guard takes it if their company has one, else the marshal (or the best
    fighter) takes it by nature (the outsiders' duel to first blood or a bout) or refuses (two goodwill). (2.8.2) hard words
    come to blows: 1 in 5 (half with the warden near) one more pair of tempers joins; the marshal near breaks it up. (2.8.3)
    first blood drawn with a bloodthirsty fighter: 1 duel in 20 goes on by the yield terms, an onlooker pulls them apart.
    (2.9.1) hard words with a notable themself, or a duel won against their people, where their ways know duels: 1 in 4
    held; 10 to 30 days on one of Rimfolk's letters by their means (the faction's age), 2 to 5 days later the challenger at
    the gate asks by name; taken by nature (the outsiders' duel) or refused (the notable's regard -6); a greetings or
    condolences letter to their people since, or a good word or a gift (`Quarrels.Eased`), settles it. (2.9.2) a head whose
    regard was -20 or worse is followed by the heir: 1 in 3 holds it four months; their visits' guards short with ours, 1
    visit in 5 a fistfight; the same letters or a gift end it. (3.8.1) an open vendetta against a people at peace: 1 visit in
    4 the avenger's fistfight. (3.13.2) a visitor of another faith and a devout of ours: 1 visit in 10 (half on best
    behavior) hard words, then the outsiders' own fistfight chance. (2.3.2) a hunger world event within reach: 1 night in
    15 two or three unarmed hungry strangers (`Arrivals.Visit`) in the fields (or the stores) for an hour; met within six
    cells, 1 in 2 a bruise, then they flee, the sack dropped; famine bread none, a night watch half, lit fields half. (2.3.3)
    two prospecting parties (visitor trips working "prospect") at once, once a rush (a "creek" marker), half the time a
    brawl between them (`Harm.Fight` with no kind: theirs), one of ours within four cells caught unless the marshal gets
    there first. Stories: (2.10.1, outside) a nemesis on the land in a fight, its victim on the field and out of cover (not
    indoors, cover blocking under two fifths): once a return it goes for them (melee or a beast straight at them, a gun to
    range), a taunt or the words over it; no Harm call, no return of its own. (3.10.2) "getting clean"'s worst night
    (stage 1, eleven to two) with the friend not within eight cells and a drug of the addiction in reach: half the time the
    game's own binge (`Binging_DrugExtreme`, else `Binging_DrugMajor`). (3.10.3) "the new leg"'s first steps (stage 0, nine
    to five), walking near the gate without the friend: 1 in 3 a fall, someone helping them up. (4.8.1) with A RimWorld of
    Magic, "the long discipline"'s long practice (stage 1): a fire, ice or storm mage (`InnerFire`, `HeartOfFrost`,
    `StormBorn`) free at dawn walks out to practise (`Rimfolk_PracticeWalk`), the teacher along when free; 1 in 25 (half
    with the teacher there) a burn, the game's frostbite (`HurtKind.Frostbite`, new) or a shock's burn. (2.6.1, outside)
    the lost one found after a night out: about half (the setting and the lean) frostnip, a chill or an ankle; a child the
    mildest (a scraped knee). (2.7.1, outside) a waylaid messenger (`CourierTracker`): half come in with two or three
    bandits of a people at war at their heels; nobody of ours within 25 cells, the cut as before and the letter's line;
    someone near, the bandits run first; the bandits run for the edge (`LordJob_ExitMapBest`), a message.
  - Messages only where the game gives one: the fights tell themselves (the game's social fight, the outsiders' brawl's

       fight or a calm answer. "the next one passed over holds it...": pick a colonist; their next two meetings.
    3. "the next council meeting boils over" with two rivals pitching; "the next gossip said to its subject's face comes to
       blows"; "the next secret let slip brings the hearer to its owner" and "the next confidence betrayed...".
    4. "the next rivals in love come to blows" (a "rival in love" at its rivals' stage); the one they like's opinion.
    5. With Ideology, the one-faith decree (its card's line), then "words at the altar at the next evening of the one faith".
    6. "the next quarrel at a day's table comes to blows" (a feast day with rivals); with Vanilla Brewing Expanded, "the next
       toast pours a second round" and "two rivals here quarrel over the second round".
    7. "the next soldier's nightmare strikes the roommate": two in one bedroom, one shaken by a nightmare (or wait for one).
    8. The open-gates decree (its card's line) and "the next open gate's visitors bring a stranger": the thief's walk to the
       stores and the chase, or the beer and the fight. Check the thief leaves with at most a small stack.
    9. "the gambler's next evening of games turns" after letting anyone play; "the barber's next cut nicks".
    10. "the next guest of rank draws an enemy" with a dignitary staying: with and without a guard in their company.
    11. "the next fistfight after hard words draws a crowd" (provoke an outsider), "the next duel to first blood goes on past
        it", "a challenge by letter for..." (the letter, then the challenger), "the next heir carries a grudge" (wait for a
        succession), "the next visit of the hated people", "zeal at the gate at the next visit".
    12. "hungry strangers in the fields tonight": the figures in the field, one of ours meeting them, the flight. "the
        prospectors here come to blows" with two parties of prospectors (a silver rush's share answer and its nugget).
    13. "the next nemesis on the land seeks the one it hurt": a raid with a nemesis, its victim in the open, then behind
        cover; a beast nemesis back for blood.
    14. "the next worst night of getting clean, alone", "the next first steps on a new leg fall", with A RimWorld of Magic
        "the next mage's practice working slips".
    15. "the next lost child is found hurt" (the mission); "the next waylaid messenger is set upon at the edge" (a letter by
        courier to a town on a dangerous road): the bandits, the cut or the flight, the message.
    16. "the shared budget (log)": the hundred listed with their passes (about 0.31).
  - Riskiest: the bandits at the edge (hostile pawns spawned beside a courier with an exit lord; they shouldn't fight, but
    the colony's drafted people can, and a hostile on the map is a threat to the game); the hungry strangers, the rank's
    challenger and the letter's challenger made with `Arrivals.Make` and `Visit`, each given a job from a lord's visit (the
    challenger seeking the colonist through `Together.When`, as the rematch's does); the nemesis's forced attack job (a
    manhunting beast's own mind may take over at once); the thief's `SplitOff` into a visitor's inventory and the drinker's
    beer made into theirs and drunk from it (`JobDefOf.Ingest` from an inventory); `MentalState_SocialFighting.otherPawn`
    and `RecoverFromState` to pull a fight apart; the binge started by name with `TryStartMentalState` (whether the game's
    binge picks the addiction's own drug is the game's); `CoverUtility.CalculateOverallBlockChance` for the nemesis's cover;
    the second round's `Ingest` jobs at a toast; the soldier's nightmare waking two at once with `EndCurrentJob`; the
    Referee's first-blood switch to yield terms mid-duel (`OutsiderOutcomes.Referee`).

    ApiDiff found nothing changed); the bite named for the animal through `Injure`'s DamageInfo (instigator and weapon set,

  - The generic catch: three hooks mark the actor (`JobDriver.TryActuallyStartNextToil`, `DriverTick`,
    `DriverTickInterval`; `[ThreadStatic]`); while one is set, an item made (`ThingMaker.MakeThing`) or dropped out of a
    building's container (`GenDrop.TryDropSpawn`: the egg box) is noted for the job, a split part (`Thing.SplitOff`) and
    anything dropped out of a pawn's hands or inventory or a corpse never. Only for a work job (a work giver), not
    ordered, of a pawn that carries; not a bill, not a job one of the sources of their own covers (plants, sowing,
    mining, the deep drill, the animals' products, taking down, floors, Odyssey's fishing), not building work. The carry
    step about to put such a thing in the hands for a storage cell takes it whole into the inventory and ends the job
    (barrels, egg boxes, the bioferrite harvester, VEF's item and pipe processors, Medieval 2's apiary, the Processor

  DESIGN.md "Medicine by what is treated" (the rule's table, the examples, both ways, the other medical mods); README

  - Code: `Health/MedicineChoiceMath.cs` (pure, linked in Tests.csproj; `MedicineChoiceTests`, "medicine by need: "):
    `Judge` (Harmless, Minor, Serious with a reason), `CareFor` (the medical care setting the ceiling), `NeedsCare`,
    `Allows`, `WithCarried`, `EndAfter`, `SameMedicineCount`, `PriorityShift`, the game's infection size curve.
    The rule: serious for the council's answer, a stage threatening life, any illness, infection or lasting condition
    but Rimfolk's everyday ailments, bleeding while the patient would bleed to death within 18 hours (the game's urgent
    mark), bleeding 40% a day or more (every fresh stump but a small creature's), a vital part (tags with `vital`: brain,
    heart, lungs, liver, kidneys, stomach, neck), an organ inside, deep (half the part's health, or 12 points on a wound
    that can go bad); minor for Rimfolk's everyday ailments, a wound bleeding 10% a day or more, or with a 3% chance or
    more of turning infected; harmless otherwise (a bruise, a crack, the smallest scratch or crush). Serious gets the
    care itself, minor herbal at most, harmless none (setting: herbal at most). Vanilla's scratches all bleed and can get
    infected, so they are minor; crushes too past the smallest. `Health/MedicineChoice.cs` (the facts from a hediff:
    the untended bleeding worked out as the game does but before tending or Field Medic's stabilizing, the infection
    chance as the game rolls it, never its hidden roll; per tick and frame caches; `CareOf`, the tendings in the game's
    order, `AfterTending`, the tooltip line, `Explain`; the book `GameComponent_MedicineChoice`),
    `Health/MedicineChoicePatches.cs`, `Health/MedicineChoiceDebug.cs`, `Integrations/SmartMedicine.cs`
    (`SmartMedicineBridge`), Keyed `Rimfolk_MedicineChoice.xml`. `DilemmaEffect_MedCare` (the doctor is the patient,
    "the best medicine for") now also calls `MedicineChoice.GaveBest`, and its sheet line names someone already on the
    best while the setting is on.

    patient); `Medicine.GetMedicineCountToFullyHeal` (only the tendings at the first's care, one at least while the game

- 0.156.0, pets hunt for themselves, and an alert for an animal with no food in reach (7 November 2026). The player's report: their
  husky Yuma was starving (the game never lets an animal it doesn't flag a predator hunt, tame animals hunt only as the
  food search's last resort, huskies can't graze, and the dog's area "Animals" left out the stores); their request, an
  explicit one: "yes, can you make animals hunt if they would do in reality, and your judgement for fictive species, and
  that they hunt what they would normally would, or hunt things below them in the food chain, not above". Not released:
  no What's new round, About.xml and CHANGELOG untouched (the lead does that at the merge). DESIGN.md "The colony's
  animals hunting for themselves" (the table of who hunts, the rule, the Pokémon, the prey rules with examples, when, harm
  beside the budget, the alert); README "The colony's animals" (two paragraphs); the Almanac's colony's animals page three
  sections (*Hunting for themselves*, *Who hunts, and what*, *No food in reach*) and Hunt for Me's page a paragraph, no
  keyword changed.
  - Code: `Animals/HuntMath.cs` (pure, linked in Tests.csproj; `HuntTests`, "pets hunting: "): `FoodChain` (prey, small
    hunter, hunter, apex), `Judge` (dryads, no food and no meat never; a Pokémon by species in its table, else a Dark type
    of 0.4+ or a Dragon type of 1+ by size, legendaries never; else the defName table, else a word of the name, last word
    first, a prey word never over the game's predator flag unless firm; else `Rule`: the flag or a meat-only diet with
    teeth by size, under 0.7 small, under 1.6 hunter), `WhyNotPrey`, `PreyLimit`, `WhyNot`, the fed hunts' pace, the
    alert's words. `Animals/PetHunts.cs` (the game's side: facts from defs, the prey search, the hungry hunt, the fed
    hunts, the short pass, the kill, the carry home, the alert's look, the button; `JobDriver_PetBringsKill`),

    `Pawn.Kill`, `Patch_PetHuntsGizmo` on `Pawn.GetGizmos`, `Alert_NoFoodInReach`), `PetHuntsDebug.cs`. `PackAlphas.Storied`
    (public, for the prey rules); `Alert_FreshCarcass` leaves a kill alone while a colony animal eats it. Defs:
    `Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_PetHunts.xml` (the job `Rimfolk_PetBringsKill`), `Defs/FlavorPoolDefs/Rimfolk_Pools_PetHunts.xml`
    (three pools, in `ImmersionTests.SpokenPools`), Keyed `Rimfolk_PetHunts.xml`. `Tools/Tests/HuntKinds.txt`: every animal
    of the base game, the DLCs (Odyssey's defs weren't to hand: its animals go by the rule) and the player's 29 animal

    119 of PokéWorld's 898).
  - No Sched slot: the short pass (the hunts kept to the rules, the alert's look, the person's line) rides on the wild's
    (`BeastBook.Rare`, every 250 ticks), the fed hunts on the people's hour (`CouncilGameComponent.HourlyPeople`), the
    hungry hunt on the game's own food search. Saved: `AnimalBook.keptHome` (the ids whose "May hunt" is off, 200 at most;
    in `Tools/save_estimate.py`). Settings: `petsHunt` ("Pets hunt for themselves", What's on, on) and `noFoodAlert` ("An
    animal with no food in reach", Alerts, on). AnimalNatureTests count four saved collections in the book now.
  - Harm: no roll of Rimfolk's own; the hunt is the game's fight (the prey picked small, weak, unlikely to turn, never
    venomous), so the shared budget doesn't count it, as it doesn't count the game's predators or the colony's hunters.
  - Try in the game (dev mode, Debug actions, Rimfolk, "Pets hunting: ..."; none of it could be run here):
    1. Select a husky (or any dog), set its area to a small one with no food in it and some hares about, then "make an
       animal hungry...": it goes after a hare inside its area (the game's "hunting" report), kills it and eats; someone in
       view says a word; its card says "caught a hare". With no prey in its area: the alert "Animal with no food in reach"
       names it with why and how to fix it, a click selects it, and its bonded person says so once.
    2. "why an animal hunts or not (log)...": its place in the food chain and why, whether it may now, its limits, and the
       twenty nearest wild animals each with why it may or may not take them.
    3. "send a hunter after small game now..." and "send a hunter to bring its person a kill...": the second carries the
       kill to its person and sets it down at their feet (their word, the thought "a present from my animal").
    4. Two dogs or wolves idle side by side, one made hungry with only an ibex or a gazelle about: both go after it.
    5. The "May hunt" button off on a hungry hunter: no hunt (the alert says it is kept); a tame wolf or cat (flagged
       predators) with nothing to eat goes by Rimfolk's rules, not the game's; the setting off: the game's own behaviour.
    6. Draft the master of a hunting dog, or let a raid come, mid-chase: it breaks off within 250 ticks; a chase that
       runs 6 cells out of its area is given up too.

    the session); Pokémon hunting depends on PokéWorld giving them melee verbs (its own melee order reads

    (`JobDriver_PetBringsKill`: an animal taking up and carrying a body, `StartCarryThing` and the drop at the person's
    feet); the revenge chance read with the hunter as instigator (three times the kind's in melee: wild Pokémon near the
    hunter's size are mostly left alone); the alert's food search each 250 ticks for each hungry animal (the game's own
    `BestFoodSourceOnMap`, reservations ignored); interplay with Hunt for Me, Animals Forage and Animals Logic (all active
    in the player's list, none read here: a food job they give always stands).

  `ImmersionTests.SpokenPools`), Keyed `Rimfolk_HarmFive.xml`. DESIGN.md "Harm, part 5" (a table of the fifteen) and "The
  rates" redone; README "Hurts from everyday life" two bullets; the Almanac's ailments page (prose only, no keyword
  changed); the review marks each built with what differs, and its Summary.
  - Registry (`HarmKinds`, founding false, base rates from the model at 4000 runs): sickWorkOn 0.020, gateSickness 0.0085,
    campFever 0.0034, courierSick 0.0026, patientIll 0.0016, badBatch 0.007, smallThings 0.008, dirtyWater 0.05 (by hand:
    the model's game hasn't Dubs Bad Hygiene's thirst, as PokéWorld's spar), gateCold 0.0018, nightWatch 0.009,
    weatherLovers 0.0005, sleepwalk 0.024, restlessWalk 0.0035, coldWater 0.028; each a system of its own in `Harm.SystemOn`
    (the two-system links behind `Interplay.On`). 48 kinds now; each passes at about 44% of its own rate.
  - The fourteen (rate on its own, prevention; seen): (1.2.5) a petition to rest when ill or for a quarantine lapsing while
    one of the colony up and about has something catching: they work on a day (`Catching.CoughHour`'s rule, now shared by
    every carrier), whoever was nearest them most catches the same a day after; named under the petition on the decree
    page. (2.3.1) a visitors' or traders' group (`LordJob_VisitColony`, `LordJob_TradeWithColony`) of a people a plague lies
    over (`Carriers.PlagueOver`, as sickness brought home reads it) carries it one in four, the trader by preference; the
    flu, the plague one in four, two or three days after they go; the plague's "shut the gate" or the quarantine decree
    keeps them out; `Council_WS_Plague`'s raised flu 1.5 to 1.35 and plague 2.5 to 2.3 make room while the carriers are
    on (`SituationModifier.withCarriers`); named under keeping the gate open. (2.7.2) a courier of such a people, the same, from `CourierTracker`'s spawn. (2.4.2) the camp's sick one
    (`Camp.FallIll`) catching one sickness in five for three days: a chest cold, the flu one in four; the doctor's tend (the
    camp's ask, its sheet says so) stops it. (3.2.2) one hospital patient in 20 brings tuberculosis or cholera (given in
    `HospitalPatient.Cast`, the letter's {TALE} names it, every answer's sheet too); a night asleep in their room 1 in 4.
    (2.2.4) one paid healer's visit in eight a bad batch, caught by a doctor of Medicine 8 (a word); one dosed in three the
    next morning: the stomach bug (tonic) or a sore arm (shot); named under paying. (3.2.3) worms untended three days 1 in
    20 the game's gut worms in their place; bites untended a day in a malaria country 1 in 20 the game's malaria (sleeves,
    a bed indoors half each). (4.9.3) Dubs Bad Hygiene's thirst ("DBHThirst") rising 0.15 in an hour is a drink; no
    treatment building of the mod's at home: the stomach bug one such day in 600, only while the mod's own water illnesses
    read off from its settings by name (unreadable: on, so nothing at all). (3.1.2) a traveller waiting at the gate past
    the hour in a hard frost (-5 °C) colder than comfortable: 1 in 20 each two hours, frostnip or chilblains; the letter
    says so in a frost. (4.2.2) the night watch on the walls (the patrol vigil): the same, half with two on watch; a lone
    watcher outside the walls (`NightWalks.OutsideWalls`: the map's edge without a closed door) with a hungry wild
    predator in reach: 1 watch in 6 its hunt; named under the watch's answer. (3.11.3) the rain lover's two hours in rain:
    a chest cold 1 day in 150; the snow lover's three in bitter falling snow: frostnip 1 in 75; a coat or a hood halves.
    (3.12.1) one nightmare in 15 that left them shaken walks them out to the yard on a later night's small hours; a bolted
    door or a roommate keeps them in; frostnip in the cold, else a stumble half the time; led back. (3.3.3) restlessness
    their strongest feeling at 1.6 its threshold: one dusk in 15 a walk to the edge of the ground (a night watch
    look-out), a friend along when free; alone outside the walls, 1 in 4 a hungry predator. (4.9.2) an hour fishing (the
    game's or Vanilla Fishing Expanded's) below freezing 1 in 200, twice in a hard frost: the game's hypothermia at
    shivering, a dash for the nearest fire.

- 0.154.2, a sick grower's full pack (7 November 2026, the player: "could it be that now if a colonist harvests a plant,
  they no longer immediately put the item into their inventory, but instead have it fall to the ground and then
  afterwards do a haul job?"). Their save: the standalone Harvest and Haul (still loaded, so Rimfolk's copy stands down)
  held Ian's load of 67 logs, full, for 195,772 ticks (three days); Ian has `Council_Ail_Tuberculosis`, and both the
  standalone and Rimfolk's copy refused any delivery while `HealthAIUtility.ShouldSeekMedicalRest`, so his pack never
  emptied and every harvest of his fell to the ground for others to haul. Rimfolk's `Carrying.CanDeliverNow` now stops
  only for a pawn lying in bed (the delivery only ever replaces work, never rest), and `HaulMath.Stuck` (three holds, a
  day at least) queues a load for storage between jobs in the rare pass whatever comes next. The standalone keeps its
  rule: the player was told to remove it, which hands its settings and the loads in the save to Rimfolk's copy. Tests:
  `FieldReportTests`. Queued as its own piece: every item work makes goes into the maker's inventory (bills, butchering,
  cooking and mods' production, as the player asked).
- 0.154.1, food for an animal never goes to a courier (7 November 2026, the player: "events/dilemmas where you provide
  food to an animal shouldn't have some courier pick up the food, that makes no sense"). 0.142.1 counted only animals
  not the colony's as an errand's receiver, but the orphaned young's "Take it in and raise it by hand"
  (`Council_Evt_OrphanedYoung`) recruits the animal before `DilemmaEffect_FeedBeast`, so the colony's own young one had
  no receiver, the errand went to the gate and `Couriers.Await` (with no people named, any friendly people's courier)
  sent someone for it. `DilemmaEffect_CarryOut.IsBeast` is now any animal, `Receiver` any animal or a stranger of
  another people, and `PlayGroups.StartCarry` walks to the colony's own animal too; the food set down is forbidden only
  for an animal not the colony's (the colony's own heeds forbidding). Tests: `FieldReportTests`.

  - Touchpoints (`Defs/IncidentDefs/Rimfolk_Events_PeoplesLore.xml`, `Defs/CampDefs/Rimfolk_CampKinds_PeoplesLore.xml`):
    the order's night nurse (`Rimfolk_Evt_OrderNurse`: a fever, from bed to bed by `VisitorServices.Dose`, hediff
    `Rimfolk_OrderNursed` in `Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_PeoplesLore_Misc.xml`, a doctor's lesson and medicine back as an option);
    the herders' young beast at the gate after a good winter's grazing; the league's winter quarters
    (`Rimfolk_Camp_LeagueWinter`); the pilgrims' Long Walk (`Rimfolk_Evt_LongWalk`, spring and summer, at the graves); the
    society's night of the fire (`Rimfolk_Evt_Disputation`, once a year); the enclave's salvage (`Rimfolk_Evt_EnclaveSalvage`,
    any age); the river folk's nets on the bank (`Rimfolk_Evt_RiverNets`). `Patches/Rimfolk_PeoplesLore.xml`: a
    herb-gatherer, a patrol, a lost traveller, a teacher and a tourist prefer the order, the league, the pilgrims, the
    society and the enclave, each with a text in their voice.
  - Faiths (all `MayRequire`, checked against the memes' exclusion tags read from Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Memes' and
    Alpha Memes' 1.6 defs, four memes at most): the order + VME light, the herders + VME elders, the league + VME
    republic, the enclave + VME progressive, the river folk + VME egalitarian; the pilgrims may take VME omnism and the
    society VME agnosticism as their structure.
  - Names: a third form of every arising name (`CC_Arise_Name_*_3`: *Lamp of Ashford*, *Ashford Waystone*, *Barr's
    Handcart*...), a second form of how seven kinds of them live (`CC_Arise_*_2`), the templates' name rules with their
    founding's words; the order's *Bell* became *Ward* (no "Quiet Bell" before that people exists).
  - Try in the game (none of it could be run here; Dev mode, Debug actions, Rimfolk's events by name, or the game's
    incident list):
    1. Open the Peoples page and a card of each of the seven (and of a people that arose): a line "They honour ..., and
       they fear ...", and "A saying of theirs: ..."; the faction page's description with the founding in its middle.
    2. Give a colonist the flu (dev: add hediff), fire `Rimfolk_Evt_OrderNurse`: a hospitaller in ivory walks in; let them
       in and watch them walk to each fevered bed (four at most), "nursed by the order" on each one's health tab, the
       outcome told when the last is seen to; the second answer with the doctor following at their side.
    3. Fire `Rimfolk_Evt_LongWalk` with and without a grave: six to nine pilgrims at the graves (or by the gate), the

    4. Fire `Rimfolk_Evt_Disputation`: the gathering that evening where the colony gathers, the fellow among them, the

    5. Fire `Rimfolk_Evt_EnclaveSalvage` in a tribal start (a runner at the gate) and an industrial one (radio): buy it,
       watch the drop pods come down by the trade spot, check their goods against the letter (steel, cloth, components,
       medicine; plasteel and chemfuel later), and the silver go to the runner or a courier.
    6. On a map with water, fire `Rimfolk_Evt_RiverNets`: two or three boatmen on the bank by the water, fish (Odyssey) or

       crated waystone at the gate. The herders' winter herd: at a good stay's end the elder walks to the gate and a young
       beast of the herd stands there, the colony's; after a bad stay (raise its unease) no walk.
    8. With Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Memes, a new world: the seven's faiths with their new memes, and no "conflicting
       memes" error in the log.
  - Riskiest: the young beast's generation (a juvenile of a modded herd animal with odd life stages; the calendar's day
    holds a pawn's id among its things); the hospitaller's rounds on a sleeping patient (the dose waits until they wake,
    twelve hours at most); the salvage's counts by `BaseMarketValue` with a market mod changing prices; the bank cell
    (dry ground next to any water, which may be a marsh or a moat); the forced memes' generation with every mod (the
    game adds forced memes without checking them, so a conflict would only show as odd precepts, hence the exclusion
    check in the test).
- 0.153.0, harm, part 4: the shared budget and fifteen more of the review (7 November 2026, the player's answer to "do more harm
  proposals raise how often colonists get hurt, or only the variety?": "yes, a shared budget please, and go ahead with the
  suggestions"; since then "all suggestions please", so the other 69 unbuilt proposals follow in later pieces on this
  budget). Not released: no What's new round, About.xml and CHANGELOG untouched (the lead does that at the merge).
  `Harm/HarmBudgetMath.cs` (the registry and the rules, `HarmBudgetTests`, "harm budget: "), `Harm/HarmFourMath.cs` (the
  fifteen's rates, `HarmFourTests`, "harm four: "), both linked in Tests.csproj and Balance.csproj; `Harm/HarmFour.cs` (the
  hub on the harm book's hour and slices), `Catching.cs`, `Mishaps.cs`, `AnimalHurts.cs`, `Quarrels.cs`, `GamesDay.cs`,
  `HarmFourDebug.cs`; `Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_HarmFour.xml` (the race's job), `Defs/FlavorPoolDefs/Rimfolk_HarmFour_Lines.xml` (29
  pools, in `ImmersionTests.SpokenPools`), Keyed `Rimfolk_HarmFour.xml`. DESIGN.md "The shared budget" and "Harm, part 4"
  (with a table of the fifteen) and "The rates" redone; README "Hurts from everyday life"; the Almanac's ailments page
  (prose only, no keyword changed) and the hail's Almanac line; the review marks each of the fifteen built with what
  differs, and its Summary.
  - The budget: every roll and every hurt through the service names its kind (`HarmKinds`: 34 now, each a key that is
    saved, a label, its system and its base rate). The founding 18 (everything built up to 0.149.0: part 1, parts 2 and 3,
    the stampede, the feasts' blow and sour night, the pilgrims' cough, the schemes' fight, the Pokémon spar) set the budget
    (their base rates summed, about 0.46 a colonist-year); a kind's chance is its base rate times `Harm.Scale` (the setting
    and the storyteller, untouched) times its pass, `HarmBudgetMath.Passes`: its variety times the budget over the kinds on
    weighed by their variety, so the kinds on always come to the budget (ceiling twice a kind's own rate). Variety: a kind
    that just hurt someone weighs a quarter of its rate, back to all of it evenly over thirty days (`HarmBook.kindLast`,
    pruned). A system off (`Harm.SystemOn`: its setting, its mod) takes its kinds out of the budget. The service's API
    changed: `Harm.Chance(kind, p)`, `Roll(kind, p)`, `Roll(pawn, kind, p, cls)`, `ScaleFor(kind)`, `PassOf(kind)`, and
    `Injure/Ail/Fight/Note` take the kind where the unused `why` string was (`Note(p, null)` counts for the cap only: the
    outsiders' practice bout, the anchor rate). Every caller updated (Dangers, the ailments, the feasts, the schemes, the
    great herds, the Pokémon spar, `Peoples/PeoplesCallers.cs`'s cough: two lines there, and its test line). The ailments
    of the land and the work never had the setting's scale and take the pass alone (`AilmentTracker.Lean`). A hunt's head
    that can turn takes its pass once a hunt, at its marking (`HuntsBite.Marked`; not up, `HarmBook.calm`, it stays calm
    under its hunters), since a pass on each shot's chance wasn't proportional.
  - How a later kind plugs in: one line in `HarmKinds` (key, label, system, base rate, `founding` false, added to `All`), a
    case in `Harm.SystemOn` if its system is new, its rolls and hurts naming it (`HarmBudgetTests` fails any call that
    doesn't), and a source in `Tools/Balance/HarmSim.cs` (`PartFourDay` is the pattern; the run prints each kind's measured
    base rate beside the registry's and flags any a quarter off, to copy in). With about 95 kinds, each passes at about a
    fifth of its own rate.
  - The fifteen (rate on its own, then prevention; seen): (1.1.1) a tending of a catching ailment, 1 in 40 (a tenth for
    tuberculosis, cholera, measles, the flu), gloves and masks, a sterile room, the quarantine or rest-when-ill decree, a
    second doctor; a day or two later with the ailment's message. (2.5.2) one visit in 20 of Rimfolk's visitors coughs;
    whoever sat with them longest catches it a day after they go. (2.2.3) out in a falling hail, 1 in 30 each 250 ticks, 2
    a storm, a bruise of 1 to 3 (children may), a helmet turns it; the hail's texts no longer say nobody is hurt. (1.2.3)
    banked fires (`DecreeHurt.ColdNights`, on its card), a night at -5 °C or colder, three hours asleep below comfort, the
    frail: a head cold one such night in seven. (4.3.1) a tree chopped by a cutter under Plants 5, 1 in 300 by the means.
    (3.4.1) a failed heavy build, 1 in 10. (4.7.2) Alpha Skills' drink before cooking or smithing, 1 in 100; new setting
    `drinkBeforeHotWork` ("A drink before hot work", Your other mods, Alpha Skills, on by default; off, no drink before hot
    work). (4.5.3) the autumn rut: a grown male grazer of 0.9 body or more in his pen with a female of his kind, a charge in
    20 hours near him, half landing; never the herdmaster. (4.5.1) the herdmaster's lesson, a nervous animal handled beside
    the learner, 1 lesson in 30. (4.9.1) Giddy-Up (its job "Mounted", by name), a dismount under Animals 6 on a mount not
    trained to obey, 1 in 50. (3.6.1) a dig at a table between groups at 60 or more, 1 in 8, two more pairs joining.
    (1.4.2) a close race's hot or bitter loser, 1 in 10 (a gracious winner's handshake at the count halves it), 1 to 3 days
    on, blows half the time. (2.5.1) a guest with a bed (Rimfolk's visitors inside; Hospitality's guests in guest beds, a
    kind of its own), 1 night in 15 by temper, the outsiders' fistfight; named under the bed's answer. (2.8.1) one beaten in
    a duel or by a bout's hard blow in 3 holds it, a rematch asked by name on a later visit within the year (a good word or
    a gift settles it; named in the duel's terms). (4.1.1) a games day's two bouts and a footrace near its gathering, 1
    bout in 25 and 1 runner in 8 on rough ground (a spacer's sim tourney: a wrenched wrist, no race); named in its letter.
  - Messages only where the game gives one for the same hurt (an illness caught: the physician, the guest's cough, the cold
    night; an animal turning on its handler: the rut, the lesson); the fights are the game's own with its message; the
    rest are seen on the map (the hit, dust or smoke, the line, a few words over them: `HarmFour.Mote`, allowed in
    TogetherTests' list of text over heads that isn't speech).
  - Game code patched (new): `Patch_FellingMishap` (a prefix and postfix on `Plant.PlantCollected`, a tree chopped) and
    `Patch_FailedBuildHurts` (a prefix and postfix on `Frame.FailConstruction`). One-line hooks in HealthPatches,
    Workers_Nature (the hail's count saved, `bruised`), CalendarKeeping, GroupMoments, OfficesElection, OutsiderOutcomes,
    VisitEffects, BeforeWork; `DrillBouts` has a games form. No Sched slot (the harm book's hour and slices).
  - Saved: `HarmBook.kindLast`, `HarmBook.waiting` (`HarmWaiting`), `HarmBook.calm`, the hail's `bruised` (all in
    `Tools/save_estimate.py`). Tests: `HarmBudgetTests`, `HarmFourTests`; the old harm tests' call texts updated (HarmTests,
    HarmTwoTests, AnimalPowersTests, BeastsTests, FeastTests, PeoplesCTests, SchemesTests, VarietyDangersTests);
    SettingsTests lists the new switch.
  - Rates (`Tools/Balance -- --harm`, 4000 runs), hurts a colonist-year, before (every kind up to 0.149.0), every kind on
    without the budget, with it: 6 well run 0.339, 0.606, 0.311; 6 average 0.453, 0.876, 0.452; 6 neglectful 0.560, 1.190,
    0.618; 12 well run 0.290, 0.483, 0.245; 12 average 0.395, 0.725, 0.368; 12 neglectful 0.504, 1.014, 0.519. The
    average colony of six (the base rates' anchor) holds; a well-run colony prevents more of the new kinds and ends a
    little lower, a neglectful one a little higher. Each kind passes at about half its rate. Variety: a kind coming again
    within thirty days 0.22 to 0.16 times a colony-year; the commonest kind's share 19.6% to 18.7%. The heart the same.
  - Try in the game (dev mode, Debug actions, Rimfolk, "Harm four: ..."; none of it could be run here):
    1. "the shared budget (log)": each kind, on or off, its base rate, days since it came, its pass (about 0.5 with every
       mod's kind on; 1 for the founding kinds if part 4's systems are all off). Cause a hurt (below), log again: that
       kind's pass drops to a quarter of the others', recovering over thirty days.
    2. "a doctor catches what a patient has...": a colonist with a head cold; within the hour (the cap allowing) the best
       doctor has it, the message naming the patient, the line over their head. In play: tend a coughing patient a few
       times.
    3. "a guest coughs...": a Rimfolk visitor (or any guest) says a cough line; sit someone by them an hour, let them go;
       a day later that colonist's head cold and its message.
    4. "a cold night for...": an elder under the banked fires decree in a frost; the next waking hour, the chill, the
       doctor's word if one is near. The decree's card shows the cold-nights line.
    5. "the next hailstone bruises": fire Rimfolk's hailstorm with someone outside: the ping, the bruise (health tab), the
       line, the words over them; a colonist in a helmet or under a roof never.
    6. "the next tree felled comes down the wrong way", "the next failed build hurts": chop a tree; fail a build (an
       unskilled builder on a wall): dust, the cutter or builder down, the line, the wound.
    7. With Alpha Skills: "a drink before hot work for..." then put them at the stove: a burn or a cut, the job dropped;
       the setting off: no drink before cooking or smithing.
    8. "a rutting male charges...": with a bull, ram or buck in a pen; the charge, the bruise, the message. In play, in
       autumn, walk someone into his pen (not the herdmaster).
    9. "the next herdmaster's lesson kicks": wait for (or start) a herdmaster's lesson with handling: the kick, the
       calming word, the message.
    10. With Giddy-Up: "the next dismount throws its rider": ride somewhere; on getting down, the buck, the fall.
    11. "two rival groups here come to blows": two of rival groups in talking range: the shove line, the fight, joiners,
        the groups' names over it. In play: a dig at supper between groups at 60.
    12. "a sore loser walks over to...": the loser finds the winner, words, blows half the time. At a close count, a kind
        or sociable winner's handshake line.
    13. "tonight's guest with a bed sours": answer a visitor's letter with a bed for the night (its sheet's health line),
        or with Hospitality guests in guest beds; after supper the fistfight; a visitor leaves at first light.
    14. "a rematch owed to...": with an outsider at peace on the map, within the hour they ask by name; the colonist takes
        it (a duel to first blood or a bout) or turns it down. In play: win a duel, let them go, wait for their people.
    15. "the games' contests now" (or keep a games day with a gathering): two bouts and a race near the gathering, the
        lines, "the next race's turn sprains" for the turned ankle; the day's letter names the contests.
    16. The setting at 0%: none of it; save and load with something waiting (a caught sickness shows after the load).
  - Riskiest: the API change touching every harm caller (built and checked by the tests' call scan, but every feature's
    chance now sits at about half its old rate, by design); the race's job and the games bouts started on pawns inside the
    games day's gathering lord (the lord takes them back after; not seen in the game); Giddy-Up's "Mounted" job read by
    name (a version that names it otherwise means no throws, never an error); the rut and the pens (`AnimalPenUtility`,
    pens' connected regions); the rematch's duel through the outsiders' private bout start (`Outsiders.Rematch` in a
    partial class); the sore loser's walk and the rematch's ask through `Together.When` (unsaved: a reload while queued
    asks again the next hour); Hospitality's guests read by their guest bed's class name.
- 0.152.0, the peoples' gear, kinds of people and gifts (7 November 2026). The
  player's report: "could it be that the new factions pawns all wear just one single outfit per faction? ... the factions
  should try to draw from all kinds of mod and vanilla references for items, weapons, gear, clothing & armor, magic and
  abilities etc." (an explicit request: no proposal round), then "if there is an army faction or so, it makes sense if
  people have more or less the same uniform ... but have variety whenever possible", "these include different xenotypes
  not just baseliners, right?" and "again, always draw from the full mod pool". It was no coincidence: every kind of the
  seven peoples had one `apparelColor` on everything and a required outfit. `docs/design/peoples.md` "Their gear, their
  kinds of people and their gifts" (how alike each role is, what they draw on, carry, their kinds of people and gifts with
  every share, the softness); DESIGN.md "Rimfolk's peoples", its last bullet; README "What the peoples wear."; the two
  peoples' Almanac pages a section each, *What they wear, carry and know* (keywords unchanged). Tests: `PeoplesGearTests`
  ("peoples' gear: "; `Peoples/PeoplesGearMath.cs` linked) against `Tools/Tests/PeopleGear.txt` (the base game's and the
  mods' gear, kinds of people, classes and paths, read from their own 1.6 defs); `PeoplesTests`' cap on other kinds of
  people raised to 35%. Nothing saved, no clock, no letter. Pawns already in a game keep what they have.
  - Gear (`Defs/PeopleDefs/Rimfolk_People_*.xml`, every PawnKindDef): no `apparelColor`; each base kind dyes its signature
    pieces by name (`specificApparelRequirements` with `apparelDef` and `color`: the order's ivory habit, plate and tabard;
    the herders' russet caps, wraps and coats; the league's teal coat and duster; the pilgrims' sage cloak; the scholars'
    claret gown, coat and jacket; the enclave's pale cyan coat and recon armour; the river folk's blue hats and coats). A
    civilian picks its signature garment by `alternateTagChoices`; soldiers wear one kit (`apparelRequired`: the sworn
    guards' plate, helmet and with Medieval 2 tabard and heater shield; the marshals' recon armour and a charge weapon;
    the league's duster, cowboy hat and flak; the wardens' helmet and cape or veil or tuque). Mods by tag or piece only
    with `MayRequire`: Vanilla Apparel Expanded and its Accessories (quivers, packs), Vanilla Armour Expanded, VFE Medieval
    2, Tribals, Settlers, Vanilla Weapons Expanded's Frontier, Non-Lethal, Grenades and Tribal sets, the rest through the
    game's tags. Medieval and tribal peoples are off `IndustrialBasic` (VAE's t-shirts and hoodies). `inventoryOptions`
    for what they carry (herbs, cloth, hay, hides, beer, books, components), never on a trader.
  - Kinds of people (each `xenotypeSet`, `Inherit="False"`): a real mix of Biotech's, Odyssey's starjack, Vanilla Races
    Expanded's (archon, lowmate, uhlan, boarskin, saurid, poluxkin, animakin, gauranlenkin, android), Alpha Genes'
    (drakonori, animusen, forsaken, lapis, nereid), Elves Continued, Stagz Merfolk, the Stoneborn, Avaloi, Boglegs and
    Venators, 21 to 29 in a hundred, the rest baseliners; each with `MayRequire` on Biotech and its mod.
  - Gifts (`PeopleKindExtension` in `Peoples/PeopleDefs.cs`, given by `Peoples/PeopleGifts.cs`, `Patch_PeopleGifts`, a
    postfix on `PawnGenerator.GenerateNewPawnInternal`, the deeper game hooks on): A RimWorld of Magic's classes by name
    (priests, paladins, druids, rangers, arcanists, chronomancers, enchanters, sharpshooters, gladiators, a commander,
    technomancers, psionics, wanderers and minstrels; only when switched on in its settings and its share for the people
    isn't 0, never a second class; its components' cached flags set back by name) and psylinks (Royalty, no letter; with
    Vanilla Psycasts Expanded a path of the kind's by name and a few of its powers, read by reflection) for the scholars
    and the enclave. Shares 3% to 45% of a kind, never more than 60%.
  - Try in the game (none of it could be run here; Dev mode, Debug actions, Rimfolk):
    1. "Peoples: their gear, kinds of people and gifts (log)..." for each of the seven: four new pawns of each kind, each
       described in the log (kind of people, what they wear with its colour, weapon, what they carry, a class or a
       psylink with its powers). The colour on one or two pieces each, the rest varied; the soldiers alike.
    2. "Peoples: one of each of their kinds here now, as visitors (testing)..." near the mouse: look them over, the sworn
       guards' tabards and shields (Medieval 2), the archers' quivers, the river folk's blue floppy hats, the enclave's
       pale cyan armour; open a class's tab on one with A RimWorld of Magic (it should fill once they are spawned), and a
